attorneys.name: Robert Carollo
attorneys.practice_type: Civil and Commercial Litigation Matters Lawyers in Clinton Township, MI
attorneys.bio:
Robert Carollo graduated from Chippewa Valley High School in Clinton Township in 2005. He obtained a Bachelor of Arts in Economics and Business in 2009 from Kalamazoo College in Kalamazoo, Michigan. Apart from his studies, Mr. Carollo was a four-year letter winner for the Kalamazoo College Division III Football Team.

In 2012, he received a Juris Doctor from the Michigan State University College of Law. He was a Captain on the Michigan State Appellate Moot Court Executive Board, ranking #12 nationally by the Law School Advocacy Group during his tenure and his team placed 2nd Overall in the John Marshall Information Technology and Privacy Law International Moot Court Competition.

Mr. Carollo began his career as a Clerk for the Honorable David Viviano of the Macomb County Circuit Court. He was also the Senior Law Clerk at the Lansing law firms Dalimonte Law, P.C. and The Senior Citizen Law Center, P.C. where he assisted in matters ranging from civil litigation to real property disputes.

In the summer of 2012, he joined the litigation team of Kirk, Huth, Lange & Badalamenti, PLC, specializing in civil and commercial litigation matters including contract disputes, personal and business tort claims, personal injury cases, probate litigation, municipal law and litigation, association, condominium law, labor and employment law, products liability and real property matters. Mr. Carollo practices at both the trial and appellate levels of the Michigan and Federal judiciary. He also routinely assists business clients with organization and formation, contract drafting, business plans, partnerships, employment agreements and pre-suit contract enforcement.

Mr. Carollo is a member of the State Bar of Michigan, the Macomb County Bar Association, and has also been admitted to practice in the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan. In his spare time he is an avid golfer and Detroit sports fan. He also is involved with the local community having assisted in coaching multiple youth sports programs in and around Clinton Township.

attorneys.bio:
David specializes in real estate, environmental, labor and employment, insurance, and business law, assisting clients with complex transactional and operational matters to optimize results and mitigate risk. David advises clients on a wide array of sophisticated matters, including management-side labor negotiations with labor unions, real estate matters, permitting and regulatory compliance, remediation and cost-recovery for contaminated properties, and corporate matters.

David helps business clients navigate the intricacies of corporate matters, contracts, litigation and trials, labor and employment disputes, enforcement and defense of non-competition agreements, real estate transactions, liquor license and regulatory matters, administrative hearings, appeals, and merger and acquisition transactions. This experience allows David to help craft effective solutions to problems business owners face that are both legally compliant and advantageous for business.

David has been selected as a Super Lawyer by his peers in environmental law.

David practiced at a large, national firm before going in-house with a private health care and insurance company as General Counsel. David joined Myers and Myers in 2025.

She serves on sophisticated and diverse matters, including real estate matters, permitting and regulatory compliance, remediation and cost-recovery for contaminated properties, and corporate matters.

For her business clients, Becky helps them navigate various aspects of ownership and operations. This includes corporate matters, contracts, litigation and trials, labor and employment disputes, enforcement and defense of non-competition agreements, real estate transactions, start-up issues, creditor actions, intellectual property and trademark applications, liquor license and regulatory matters, administrative hearings, appeals, and sale and merger transactions. With this business-based, common-sense approach, Becky frequently acts as her clients' "in-house counsel," often consulting on their operational legal concerns and working with their other professional service providers to achieve their goals.

As a respected member of the legal community, Becky also serves as a case evaluator and neutral mediator to help others resolve their legal disputes. Becky has been selected as a Super Lawyers Rising Star by her peers and also received an AV Preeminent rating by Martindale-Hubbell, being peer-rated and judicially rated for the highest level of professional excellence and ethical standing.

Becky practiced at a large, national firm before joining Myers & Myers, PLLC in 2011. In 2010 and again each year in 2013-2020, she has been selected as a Super Lawyers Rising Star, which is an exclusive list of top-rated attorneys in specific practice areas who were chosen after nomination by their peers and thorough evaluation of numerous criteria. Becky also received an AV Preeminent rating by Martindale-Hubbell, being peer-rated and judicially rated for the highest level of professional excellence and ethical standing.

Becky uses her breadth of experience, professionalism, and standing in the community to achieve favorable results for her clients.

attorneys.name: Paul O. Catenacci
attorneys.firm_name: Novara Tesija Catenacci McDonald & Baas PLLC
attorneys.practice_type: Employee Benefits Law Lawyers in Southfield, MI
attorneys.bio:
Background: Mr. Catenacci joined the firm in 2008 and became a partner in 2014. Mr. Catenacci focuses his practice on the representation of multiemployer employee benefit plans, with a particular emphasis on health and welfare plans. Mr. Catenacci has extensive experience with the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act (PPACA) and advises clients on the full range of issues that affect health and welfare plans, including plan design, plan drafting, appeals and appeals procedures, plan mergers, preparation of Summary Plan Descriptions, as well as general compliance with the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA), the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA), and the Internal Revenue Code (IRC).

Mr. Catenacci also represents various clients with respect to complex alternative investments. He regularly works with Qualified Plan Asset Managers (QPAMs), Venture Capital Operating Companies (VCOCs), Real Estate Operating Companies (REOCs) and Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs), as well as fund of funds investment vehicles employing master/feeder structures. Mr. Catenacci has experience with representing borrowers and lenders relative to construction financing, loan restructuring, and commercial lease agreements.

In addition, in connection with his representation of multiemployer plans, Mr. Catenacci routinely deals with collection matters related to fringe benefit delinquencies. He has extensive experience with not only standard delinquencies, but also collection actions involving the use of alter ego/"double-breasted" structures by signatory employers. Mr. Catenacci has litigated these matters in a variety of federal district courts, as well as in the Court of Appeals for the 6th Circuit.

Prior to joining the firm, Mr. Catenacci was employed in a national security related position where he held a Top Secret/SCI Security Clearance.

Education: Mr. Catenacci earned his Juris Doctorate from Wayne State University School of Law. He completed his undergraduate work at the University of Michigan at Ann Arbor.

Professional Affiliations: Mr. Catenacci is a member of the International Foundation of Employee Benefit Plans (IFEBP), the Michigan Association of Public Employee Retirement Systems (MAPERS), as well as the American Bar Association (ABA) and the Michigan State Bar. Mr. Catenacci is admitted to practice before the United States Court of Appeals for the 6th Circuit, the Federal District Courts for the Eastern and Western Districts of Michigan, as well as the Federal District Court for the Northern District of Ohio.

attorneys.name: Gerald P. Cavellier
attorneys.practice_type: Matrimonial Law Lawyers in Bloomfield Hills, MI
attorneys.bio:
Gerald P. Cavellier is the head of the Domestic Relations/Family Law Section at Hertz Schram PC. He is a graduate of Michigan State University College of Law (formerly known as the Detroit College of Law). His entire practice focuses on Family Law matters. Mr. Cavellier is a litigator at heart, but he is also trained in Mediation and is a member in good standing with the Family Mediation Counsel of Michigan. He is a past Chair of the Oakland County Family Law Committee, a member of the Family Law Section of the State Bar of Michigan and is currently a Professor of Law at Western Michigan University Cooley Law School teaching Family Law. His practice involves all aspects of family law including Custody, Child Support, Parenting Time, Spousal Support, and Property Division. He is also very familiar with more complex issues including marital tort litigation, division of closely held businesses, alienation of children and interstate custody and support issues. Mr. Cavellier is that special type of lawyer who is capable of handling very personal, emotional matters, yet he knows when to zealously advocate or aggressively negotiate.

attorneys.name: Charles E. Chamberlain Jr.
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Grand Rapids, MI
attorneys.bio:
Attorney and founding firm partner Charles E. Chamberlain, Jr. has been practicing law in West Michigan for over 30 years. His legal practice has covered a wide variety of trial work in both federal and state courts. Early in his career, "Chip" Chamberlain was a federal prosecutor, as well as a defense attorney.

Chip has earned an excellent reputation among fellow attorneys and judges, and is known as a tough and effective advocate for his clients. He is a fellow of the American and Michigan Bar Foundations. He has also been listed in The Best Lawyers in America every year since 2000, and in Michigan Super Lawyers since 2006. The Grand Rapids Magazine has also recognized him as one of Michigan's top lawyers.

If you have been charged with a crime, you need aggressive, effective and efficient representation dedicated to protecting your rights and interests at every stage of your case. Experienced attorney Chip Chamberlain will effectively support you from the grand jury investigation through an appeal, if necessary.

For more information about criminal defense attorney Chip Chamberlain, or to learn more about the experienced and trusted criminal defense attorneys at Willey & Chamberlain, contact us here or call our office directly at 616.458.2212.

attorneys.name: Michael S. Cheltenham
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in East Lansing, MI
attorneys.bio:
Mike Cheltenham is a distinguished alumnus of the University of Michigan, Ann Arbor, and holds a Juris Doctor degree from Wayne State University Law School. With a rich professional background, he currently serves as Of Counsel at Cheltenham Law, PLLC, specializing in criminal defense throughout Mid-Michigan.

Leveraging Prosecution Experience for Your Defense

Mike's journey in the criminal law spans over two decades, including his tenure as Chief Assistant Prosecuting Attorney for the Ingham County Prosecutor’s Office. This extensive prosecutorial experience is a unique asset in defending criminal cases. Here's why it benefits you:

Insider Knowledge: Having been on the other side, Mike understands the strategies and tactics prosecutors use. This insight allows him to anticipate their moves and develop robust defense strategies to counteract them.

Strong Relationships: Mike’s long-standing relationships with law enforcement and other legal professionals can facilitate smoother negotiations and more favorable outcomes for his clients.

Comprehensive Case Analysis: His experience in prosecuting complex cases, including those involving child abuse, sexual assault, and narcotics, means he can scrutinize every detail of your case to identify weaknesses in the prosecution’s arguments.

Proven Leadership: As a supervising attorney, Mike oversaw numerous cases and legal personnel, honing his ability to manage and navigate the intricacies of the legal system effectively.

Extensive Legal Expertise

During his years at the Ingham County Prosecutor’s Office, Mike held supervisory roles in:

Child Abuse/Sexual Assault Unit (criminal sexual conduct involving minors, computer sex crimes, and child abuse)

District Court Unit (domestic violence, drunk driving, traffic offenses, and assaults)

Circuit Court Unit (low level felony offenses to capital crimes including armed robbery and murder)

Tri-County Metro Narcotics Unit (delivery, possession, and possession with intent to deliver cocaine, heroin, fentanyl, meth, and other various controlled substances)

In these positions, he gained expertise across the spectrum of criminal law. This experience gave him a deep understanding of both the prosecutorial process and the importance of a vigorous defense to protect a defendant’s rights and vindicate the wrongly accused.

Started in Criminal Defense

Before his impressive career at the prosecutor’s office, Mike dedicated himself to criminal defense in Northern Michigan, representing indigent clients facing felony charges in Alpena, Montmorency, Alcona, and Presque Ilse counties.

Educator and Mentor

In addition to his legal practice, Mike has shared his wealth of knowledge and experience as an Adjunct Professor at Western Michigan University Thomas M. Cooley Law School, where he taught trial skills for 13 years. As a professor he instructed students in the nuances of trial advocacy, public speaking, and courtroom persuasion.

Contact Us

If you are facing criminal charges and need an experienced defense attorney who can leverage insider prosecutorial knowledge for your benefit, contact Mike Cheltenham at Cheltenham Law, PLLC. Let our expertise and dedication work for you.

attorneys.name: Colline Cheltenham
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in East Lansing, MI
attorneys.bio:
Your Family Law and Litigation Attorney

Colline Cheltenham: Colline Cheltenham is the Managing Attorney at Cheltenham Law, PLLC, where she not only oversees the operations of the firm but also balances her role as a dedicated mother of two and wife. Specializing in family law throughout Mid-Michigan, Ms. Cheltenham brings her extensive experience to a variety of legal areas, including estate planning, driver’s license restoration, and personal injury cases.

A graduate of Northwood University with a degree in Business Administration, Ms. Cheltenham also holds a Juris Doctor degree from Thomas M. Cooley Law School. Her diverse legal knowledge and strong business acumen position her as a trusted advisor and advocate for her clients.

EXPERIENCE MATTERS:

Ms. Cheltenham’s journey in family law began years ago as a paralegal, where she gained invaluable insight into the intricacies of family law. Through hands-on experience and relentless dedication, she developed a deep understanding of the demands of private practice, particularly in the field of family law.

Today, Ms. Cheltenham is recognized as a highly respected family law litigation attorney, known for her commitment to continuing education. She actively participates in in-person and online training programs through the Institute for Continuing Legal Education (ICLE), staying up-to-date on the latest developments in family law, civil litigation, estate planning, and personal injury law.

Complex Issues Are Her Specialty: Ms. Cheltenham has earned a reputation for handling particularly challenging family law cases, many of which other attorneys may shy away from. Her focus over the last decade has been on complex divorce cases, intricate custody disputes—often involving sensitive issues such as parental alienation and emotional abuse.

Additionally, Ms. Cheltenham has achieved notable success in Estate Plan drafting, driver’s license restoration cases and personal injury.

Her client base primarily spans Ingham, Kent, Eaton, Clinton, Shiawassee, and Isabella counties, though she represents clients across the entire state of Michigan.

Straight Forward and Honest: Known for her no-nonsense approach, Ms. Cheltenham is a skilled litigator who communicates clearly and directly with her clients. She is unwavering in her determination to fight for the best possible outcomes in difficult legal battles. Her compassion for her clients is evident in her work with fathers seeking to regain their parental rights, as well as women who have endured domestic violence, financial, and emotional abuse.

Active Community Involvement: Outside of her legal practice, Ms. Cheltenham is actively engaged in the legal community as a member of the Ingham County Bar Family Law Section, the State Bar of Michigan Family Law Section, and the American Bar Association Family Law Division. In addition, Ms. Cheltenham enjoys the simple pleasure of life like horseback riding, skiing, boating, golf and reading.

LEGAL EXPERTISE

Ms. Cheltenham is admitted to practice in Michigan’s Circuit Courts, as well as federal courts, including the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Michigan and the United States Supreme Court.

Throughout her years of practice, Ms. Cheltenham has become particularly skilled in the following areas:

Complex Divorce Cases with Significant Assets: Ms. Cheltenham is adept at navigating financially complex divorce cases, having handled numerous high-net-worth divorces. She skillfully advocates for fair settlements and creatively works to reduce her clients' financial obligations while securing an equitable distribution of the marital estate.

Complex Custody Cases: Custody cases often involve challenging issues, particularly when emotional abuse or parental alienation is at play. Ms. Cheltenham works closely with experts who can testify on these matters, providing critical evidence that can change the course of a case.

Estate Planning: Estate planning can be a complex process, but Ms. Cheltenham simplifies it for her clients. She tailors estate plans to meet each client’s needs, whether drafting a simple will or a more complex trust, ensuring that her clients’ wishes are honored and their assets are safeguarded.

Personal Injury: In personal injury cases, Ms. Cheltenham is known for her legal tenacity and advocacy in the courtroom. She is committed to securing the best possible outcomes for her clients, ensuring they receive fair compensation for their injuries.

Britt is a conscientious, caring, and detail-oriented legal advisor. She puts clients at ease with her positive attitude, her warmth, and her penchant for problem solving.

Aside from her passion for the law, Britt enjoys being with her husband and kids, being outdoors, cooking, and playing the guitar.

attorneys.firm_name: Law Offices of Jeffery A. Cojocar, PC
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Commercial Law Lawyers in Shelby Township, MI
attorneys.bio:
For his undergraduate work, Mr. Cojocar attended Wayne State University; he completed a major in political science and a complimentary minor in criminal justice. After graduation, he enrolled at the Florida State University College Of Law. During law school, he took part in clinical externships at both the First District Court of Appeals for the Honorable William Benton, III and at the Jefferson County State Attorney's Office, handling all areas of criminal prosecutions on behalf of the state of Florida.

Upon graduation from law school in 1995, Mr. Cojocar moved back to Michigan, took and passed the Michigan State Bar Examination and began his legal practice career at a small litigation firm in Sterling Heights, Michigan. In 1998 he started his own practice, which he has actively pursued since that time period.

Jeffery Cojocar has served as a Director on the Young Lawyers Section Board of Directors of the Macomb County Bar Association for five of the last six years. He is also a proud member of the Oakland County Bar Association's American Inn of Court and is an active member of several other professional organizations including the following:

State Bar of Michigan

Macomb County Bar Association

Oakland County Bar Association

Michigan Trial Lawyers Association

State Appellate Defender Office (SADO) Forum

Criminal Defense Attorneys Association of Michigan

American Association for Justice

American Inns of Court

Institute of Continuing Legal Education

Jeff Cojocar practices mainly in the Tri-County area of Macomb, Oakland and Wayne counties located in southeastern Michigan, near Detroit. He has, however, litigated cases throughout Michigan including cases in the counties of Lapeer, St. Clair, Sanilac, Saginaw, Midland, Ingham, Bay, Washtenaw, Genesee, Montmorency and Calhoun. Mr. Cojocar is admitted to practice in all state courts throughout the State of Michigan, as well as the Second Circuit Court of Appeals in Cincinnati, Ohio, and the U.S District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan in Detroit, Michigan.

Mr. Cojocar has authored a number of articles on legal topics [link to Articles] He routinely attends Continuing Legal Education courses and seminars and has been a speaker at many of these seminars as well.

Jeffery A. Cojocar is an attorney committed to giving clients the service they expect and deserve. He works hard and prides himself on his excellent communications skills - clients are never out of the loop. He has instilled in his staff the values that make for a good law firm-client relationship, like good service, reliability, honesty and hard work. At the firm, we strive to provide clients with knowledgeable, zealous legal representation thus meeting our clients' needs in an efficient and expeditious manner. Give us a call to discuss our qualifications to represent you.

attorneys.name: A. Vince Colella
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Southfield, MI
attorneys.bio:
Respected by lawyers and judges as an aggressive, skillful, and powerful trial lawyer, and by his clients as a compassionate and relentless advocate, A. Vince Colella is a founding partner of Moss & Colella, P.C., a Southfield, Michigan-based law firm that specializes in personal injury trial law and civil rights. Vince and his law firm co-founder David Moss have obtained millions of dollars in verdicts and settlements for their clients. For more than two decades, Vince has tried and won cases in state and federal courts throughout Michigan.

Vince takes public sector accountability to a higher level in pursuing justice for victims and their families in civil rights cases, including police shootings, police brutality, deadly force, jailhouse deaths, and premises liability at bars and lounges where death or severe injury has occurred. He has a growing national reputation for taking on tough cases, including the fatal shooting of a 31-year-old unarmed woman by a City of Dearborn Police Officer; a man who was shot and killed by a St. Clair Shores police officer; the shooting of an unarmed teen by a Royal Oak, Michigan police officer; the shooting of a mentally ill man by a Harris County (Texas) Deputy Sheriff; and the ultimate death of a man in a Mt. Clemens, Michigan bar who died following a blow to the head as the security guard watched.

A thought leader in personal injury and civil rights, Vince’s insights are frequently sought by media outlets including the Detroit News, Detroit Free Press, WWJ News Radio 950, Fox2 Detroit, Crain’s Detroit Business, Michigan Lawyers Weekly, and Law 360. He also writes a monthly legal column, Colella in Context, in the Detroit Legal News, exploring such topics as the need to eliminate qualified immunity for police officers.

attorneys.name: Howard H. Collens
attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Huntington Woods, MI
attorneys.bio:
Howard H. Collens, as an attorney and counselor, listens to his clients, understands their goals and offers creative, effective solutions to meet their needs.

He advises clients in estate planning for estates of every size. Focusing on the unique aspects of each representation, Mr. Collens tailors trusts, wills and powers of attorney to meet the present and changing needs of his clients.

Mr. Collens is a trusted counselor for those seeking representation for estate administration. He helps families following the death of a loved one as they navigate the complexities of the probate process or trust administration. He regularly guides his clients through the sale, distribution, of real estate holdings by probate and trust estates. With litigation experience in the probate courts throughout metropolitan Detroit, Mr. Collens is a strong advocate for those involved in contested estates, trusts or other probate cases.

With understanding and compassion, Mr. Collens assists individuals and their families in planning for their long-term care needs. He eases the process of applying for and obtaining Medicaid benefits to pay for such care. Since estate recovery is a reality for those receiving long-term care in Michigan, proper titling of real estate is even more important today than ever.

Howard H. Collens is a founding member of Collens Estate Law. Mr. Collens focuses his practice on contested and uncontested probate and trust administration, guardianships and conservatorships, estate planning, and elder law. He is a member of the State Bar of Michigan’s Elder Law and Disability Rights Section. He is serving in his second stint as a member of the ELDRS’s Council and is a member of the ELDRS’s legislative committee. He is a member of the State Bar of Michigan’s Probate and Estate Planning Section. He serves on the PEPS’s Legislative Development and Drafting Committee. He is a member of ICLE’s Elder Law Advisory Board. He has completed ICLE's Probate and Estate Planning Certificate Program. He is a member of the Wayne County Probate Bar Association, Oakland County Bar Association, and the Macomb County Probate Bar Association. He serves as a member of the Board of the Area Agency on Aging 1B -Ageways. He is a trustee of the Royal Oak Civic Foundation. He is a former chair of the Huntington Woods Senior Advisory Committee and former president of the Royal Oak Chamber of Commerce Board of Directors. He has been selected as a Super Lawyer each year from 2019 to 2024 including being recognized as one of the Top 100 Lawyers in Michigan in 2023 and 2024. Mr. Collens speaks regularly on topics of fiduciary access to digital assets, remote witnessing and remote notarization, estate planning, and estate administration.

sections.title: Overview
sections.content:
Howard H. Collens, as an attorney and counselor, listens to his clients, understands their goals and offers creative, effective solutions to meet their needs.

He advises clients in estate planning for estates of every size. Focusing on the unique aspects of each representation, Mr. Collens tailors trusts, wills and powers of attorney to meet the present and changing needs of his clients.

Mr. Collens is a trusted counselor for those seeking representation for estate administration. He helps families following the death of a loved one as they navigate the complexities of the probate process or trust administration. He regularly guides his clients through the sale, distribution, of real estate holdings by probate and trust estates. With litigation experience in the probate courts throughout metropolitan Detroit, Mr. Collens is a strong advocate for those involved in contested estates, trusts or other probate cases.

With understanding and compassion, Mr. Collens assists individuals and their families in planning for their long-term care needs. He eases the process of applying for and obtaining Medicaid benefits to pay for such care. Since estate recovery is a reality for those receiving long-term care in Michigan, proper titling of real estate is even more important today than ever.

Howard H. Collens is a founding member of Collens Estate Law. Mr. Collens focuses his practice on contested and uncontested probate and trust administration, guardianships and conservatorships, estate planning, and elder law. He is a member of the State Bar of Michigan’s Elder Law and Disability Rights Section. He is serving in his second stint as a member of the ELDRS’s Council and is a member of the ELDRS’s legislative committee. He is a member of the State Bar of Michigan’s Probate and Estate Planning Section. He serves on the PEPS’s Legislative Development and Drafting Committee. He is a member of ICLE’s Elder Law Advisory Board. He has completed ICLE's Probate and Estate Planning Certificate Program. He is a member of the Wayne County Probate Bar Association, Oakland County Bar Association, and the Macomb County Probate Bar Association. He serves as a member of the Board of the Area Agency on Aging 1B -Ageways. He is a trustee of the Royal Oak Civic Foundation. He is a former chair of the Huntington Woods Senior Advisory Committee and former president of the Royal Oak Chamber of Commerce Board of Directors. He has been selected as a Super Lawyer each year from 2019 to 2024 including being recognized as one of the Top 100 Lawyers in Michigan in 2023 and 2024. Mr. Collens speaks regularly on topics of fiduciary access to digital assets, remote witnessing and remote notarization, estate planning, and estate administration.

attorneys.name: Dana M. Constand
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Grosse Pointe Farms, MI
attorneys.bio:
Experience

A special level of care and consideration is required when family life intersects with the law. Dana M. Constand created Family Focus Law to provide family focused legal services. It's about family- your family. You need an attorney to guide you through the unfamiliar territory. Ms. Constand practices in the areas of law that most often touch family life. Clients of Family Focus Law receive the benefit of individualized attention and expertise needed to help them resolve even the most complex family law matters.

Education & Experience

Ms. Constand earned her Juris Doctor Law Degree in 2014, at the Thomas M. Cooley School of Law. She received a Bachelor of Fine Arts from the University of Michigan in 1991. Ms. Constand began solo practice in 2014, initially focusing on family law. She expanded her practice to include adoption, probate administration, guardianship and conservatorship law as these areas naturally overlap with family law. Ms. Constand provides representation for family law matters, including divorce, custody, parenting time, child support, spousal support, father's rights (paternity),adoption, probate administration, guardianship and conservatorship, as well as other family related issues. Always striving for excellence, Ms. Constand participates in several industry associations, including the Family Law Section of the State of Michigan Bar Association.

Important life decisions that affect your future and that of your children, your parents and grandparents, call for knowledgeable, careful guidance. Clients can expect prompt communication, respectful treatment and informed, diligent work on their behalf. Your story and your goals are carefully considered in assessing your needs and planning the approach to solving your legal issues. Get the legal advice, counsel and representation you deserve from an attorney who understands the depth and delicate nature of legal issues surrounding family. Contact Dana M. Constand of Family Focus Law, located in Grosse Pointe Farms, Michigan.

Before Dana Was a Lawyer

Prior to pursuing a career in law, and continuing to this day, Dana is a folk artist painter, creating primarily in watercolor. Dana's art work is represented by Hanni Gallery in Harbor Springs Michigan. See https://hannigallery.com/collections/all

I have also had several of my settlements and verdicts published in the Michigan Lawyers Weekly including the annual Million Dollar Verdicts and Settlements. I handle all types of injury claims with an emphasis on wrongful death cases. My practice currently consists of about 80% medical malpractice cases and 20% automobile negligence, automobile No Fault claims, and general negligence cases. I am available for a free consultation over the phone or in person concerning any personal injury matter and all cases that I accept are done on a contingency fee basis.

attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Muskegon, MI
attorneys.bio:
Shon Cook is passionate about the law and helping clients reach the best possible outcomes. With over 30 years of experience, she has represented individuals in nearly every area of the law.

Today, she focuses exclusively on family law, handling complex and high-asset divorce, custody and parenting time disputes, spousal support, guardianships, prenuptial and postnuptial agreements, collaborative law, and mediation.

Her philosophy is simple: use the power of the law to make a positive difference in people’s lives.

In addition to her legal practice, Shon is a respected speaker for the State Bar of Michigan and the Institute of Continuing Legal Education. She helps train attorneys and Judges across the state on critical issues affecting families and the division of assets.

Outside of work, Shon has coached countless youth soccer, softball, and basketball teams in the Whitehall area. She’s raised three children, owned three law firms, and run three marathons (so far)—her personal “trifecta” of accomplishments.

Ann Cooper graduated from Michigan State University, Byrn Mawr College, and the University of Michigan Law School. She was a Fulbright Scholar in France. She has practiced in Michigan courts and in the eastern and western districts of Michigan's federal courts. Ms. Cooper served on the United States 6th Circuit Judicial Merit Selection Panel in 1998.

attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Plymouth, MI
attorneys.bio:
Since graduating from the University of Michigan Law School, Sarah Creem practiced family law first in Portland, Oregon and now in Michigan. Sarah is the former chair of the Oregon Trial Lawyers Association, Family Law Section.

Sarah is grateful for her many years at one of the largest family law firms in the country, Gevurtz, Menashe, PC. While there, Sarah was the lead attorney on hundreds of cases. She was a sought-after attorney, known for both negotiating advantageous settlements for her clients and crafting winning arguments in the courtroom. Sarah has extensive experience with complex and difficult family law cases.

Sarah approaches each case with an eye toward minimizing the negativity and stress for the client and the family as a whole. She stands in the gap for clients who are unable to stand up themselves, who are worn down by the conflict. Sarah has a heart for protecting children and taking care in cases to minimize the effects of the divorce on them.

Sarah Creem was born and raised in a family of eight in the suburbs of Detroit, Michigan. She loves her family, traveling, supporting foster kids and their foster families, and outdoor recreation. Sarah is an active member of Ward Church in Northville. Downtown Plymouth is where Sarah now calls home, along with her husband, three children, and fun-loving cat.

In the estate planning area, Lindsay delivers creative solutions to families, professionals (including dentists and health care providers), and high-wealth individuals, to help achieve financial goals while minimizing any potential tax burdens. Through wills, trusts, advanced directives, guardianships, conservatorships, LLCs, and other vehicles, she gives clients peace of mind that their heirs and beneficiaries will be well taken care of when they are gone or cannot make decisions for themselves. attorneys.name: Charles R. Cuzydlo
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Okemos, MI
attorneys.bio:
Chuck Cuzydlo is an incisive advocate representing clients in the areas of real estate, bankruptcy, estate planning and family law. Cuzydlo Law Group, PLLC is a full-service law firm that focuses on achieving strong results for his clients. In the corporate arena, Mr. Cuzydlo represents businesses from formation to litigation. As a former in-house attorney for a health care organization, he has expertise with health and healthcare law. His work in the healthcare area includes a particular focus on billing fraud and abuse and medical staff issues.

Getting to know Chuck Cuzydlo . . .

I became a lawyer because. . . I was helped by a lawyer when I was injured in a car accident as a child. His help was invaluable to my family and focused my attention the importance of the law to all of us. Actually, the compensation for this accident put me through college.

What I like most about the law is. . . exceeding my client's expectations.

My most rewarding case was. . . a large corporate client of ours was sued for over $30 million. After extensive discovery, the Plaintiff's case was completely dismissed in our favor.

I founded Cuzydlo Law Group, PLLC because. . . I believed my clients should be treated with candor and respect - traits not commonly found in law firms.

What makes Cuzydlo Law Group, PLLC different from other lawyers? We treat our clients as equals and partners in their case.

I was honored to be described as . . . "One of the best young attorneys in town" by a local business leader.

Someone I really admire is. . . my father - he really worked hard to support our family.

My favorite quote is. . . "The harder you work, the luckier you are."

When not at work, I enjoy. . . spending time with my family and winter skiing.

attorneys.name: Meredith E. Dahlen
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Plymouth, MI
attorneys.bio:
I am a family law attorney, mediator, and collaborative practitioner. I am also a proud Spartan, Wolverine, and Warrior! I earned my Bachelor's in Social Work from Michigan State University in 2007 and my law degree from Wayne State University Law School in 2010. I went on to earn my Master of Social Work from the University of Michigan in 2011, in the practice method of Social Policy and Evaluation, and the practice area of Children and Youth in Families and Society. While pursuing my MSW, I had the opportunity to assist in starting a specialty court docket called the Baby Court project, promoting stability and expedited reunification or permanency for our youngest children in foster care.

I began my legal career as a staff attorney at the Detroit Center for Family Advocacy (CFA), where I focused on the intersection between child welfare and family law matters. I worked to keep children out of the foster care system, remaining with their families whenever possible, and advocated for children in foster care to be raised in stable, safe environments, surrounded by family or other loving caregivers.

I then went on to work for the State Court Administrative Office, the administrative arm of the Michigan Supreme Court. I worked as a Friend of the Court Bureau Management Analyst, exploring new ways for courts to provide holistic, innovative services to families.

My practice philosophy is to utilize various creative methods of alternative dispute resolution to assist families in reaching resolutions that emphasize efficiency, compromise, and longevity. Whether I am representing one party or acting as a neutral facilitator for both parties, I encourage families to work together, resolving matters outside of the courtroom whenever possible. I believe in empowering families to keep decision-making in their own hands, because no one knows what is best for a family than the family itself.

She graduated from Michigan State University with Honors in 1993, where she obtained her Bachelor of Arts in General Business Administration-Prelaw and was a member of the Spartan Marching Band and Spartan Brass. Ms. Danner-Bond earned her Juris Doctorate from the University of Detroit Mercy School of Law in 1997, where she was the Managing Editor of the University of Detroit Mercy Law Review and a member of the American Inn of Court. Prior to joining the Firm in 2004, Ms. Danner-Bond practiced estate planning, probate, and tax law with a firm in downtown Ann Arbor.

In addition to being certified in probate and estate planning law by The Institute of Continuing Legal Education, Ms. DannerBond has extensive experience in Community Association Law. She handles assessment collection matters, lien foreclosure, bylaw enforcement, governing document amendments, as well as FHA certification issues. Ms. Danner-Bond has presented lectures on Community Association topics for United Condominium Owners of Michigan, the Michigan Chapter of the Condominium Association Institute, and the Firm's Condominium and HOA Board Education and Training (B.E.A.T.) program.

Ms. Danner-Bond has been licensed to practice law in Michigan since 1998 and is admitted to practice before the United States Federal District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan and the United States Tax Court. Ms. Danner-Bond served 8 years on the Board of Directors for her own condominium association in Canton, Michigan. This first-hand experience as a Co-owner and Director, in addition to being a Community Association Attorney, allows her to relate well to the many challenges that Community Association Boards face each day. Ms. Danner-Bond resides in Plymouth with her husband, two children, and their rescue dog. She has numerous interests, including spending time with family and friends, riding her Harley, reading (and listening to audio books), cooking, and traveling.

attorneys.name: Adil Daudi J.D.
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Okemos, MI
attorneys.bio:
Adil Daudi is a Partner at Daudi & Kroll, P.C., specializing in Business Law, Mergers & Acquisitions, and Estate Planning, including Shariah compliant strategies. Acting as general counsel for numerous businesses, ranging from start-ups and non-profits to large corporations, Adil offers strategic legal guidance across a wide array of matters. His expertise includes corporate governance, franchise development, operating agreements, corporate restructuring, and succession planning, making him a vital resource for navigating both routine and complex transactions.

Known for his creativity and ability to think outside the box, Adil excels in developing and implementing innovative solutions customized to his clients' needs. Whether navigating business deals, drafting governance documents, or advising on non-profit compliance, he brings a practical and strategic approach to every matter.

In estate planning, Adil works closely with individuals and families to design comprehensive plans that preserve and transfer wealth seamlessly across generations. He also specializes in Shariah compliant estate planning, ensuring that clients’ assets are distributed in accordance with Islamic principles while also meeting legal requirements. His ability to integrate both traditional and Shariah compliant strategies make him uniquely equipped to serve a diverse range of clients. Adil’s attention to detail and personalized approach ensure that his clients’ long-term goals are fully realized and protected.

Adil’s blend of sharp intellect, creative problem solving, and client centric focus make him an invaluable partner, whether assisting businesses, non-profits, or individuals with their most critical legal matters.

attorneys.bio:
A significant part of Attorney Robert C. Davis' legal practice is his "of counsel" relationship with THE WOLF LAW FIRM. Mr. Davis, in his of counsel role, handles sophisticated litigation and appeals.

Mr. Davis has extensive experience in environmental law, including clean-up strategies, agency disputes, general compliance and auditing, permitting and all related litigation.

For six year, he taught the Law of Hazardous Waste and Michigan Water Law at the University of Detroit Merey School of Law.

He is sought after on environmental topics, including water damage and mold claims for the construction industry. He also is a noted trial and appellate litigator in business, zoning and land use matters.

Prior to becoming an attorney, Mr. Davis served as lieutenant in the U.S. Coast Guard Detroit District Office as Chief of Pollution Response.

attorneys.name: Tiffany DeBruin
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in East Lansing, MI
attorneys.bio:
Tiffany DeBruin grew up in a small town in Ohio. She attended Malone University, where she earned her bachelor’s degree in Business Administration in 2003. She went on to complete her law degree at Capital University Law School in 2006. After practicing law in Ohio for five years, Tiffany moved to Michigan with her husband. In 2011, she founded DeBruin Law, PLLC, and has been running her solo practice ever since. She enjoys the work she does and finds real purpose in helping her clients.

Approach To Criminal Defense

Tiffany builds strong defense strategies for each and every one of her clients. She works hard to protect their rights and focus on the person behind the case. When clients cannot appear in person in Lansing, she communicates clearly with them and takes the lead in court. She often works with parents of college students and clients from out of town. Her goal is to handle everything thoroughly and with as little stress as possible, so her clients can move forward with their lives.

Philosophy And Personal Commitment

Tiffany is committed to fiercely advocating for every client with respect and integrity. She listens carefully to her clients and takes time to explain their options. She treats every case seriously and works hard to protect the rights of every person she represents. Her passion for defense work ties closely to the values she learned growing up in Ohio. Tiffany takes pride in standing up for people when they need help the most.

Client Success Stories

Tiffany has helped many clients reach favorable outcomes. Some examples of her success stories include:

Dismissal of embezzlement charges involving over $100,000

Reduction of a carrying concealed weapon charge to a minor misdemeanor

Full dismissal of malicious destruction of property charges

Dismissal of assault with intent to do great bodily harm charges before probable cause conference

Acquittal in a domestic violence case

Dismissal of battery and domestic violence charges

Reduction of commercial driving violations to non-abstractable infractions

Reduction of OWI charges for an underage client to a non-alcohol-related offense

attorneys.name: Stephen M. Denenfeld
attorneys.practice_type: Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Kalamazoo, MI
attorneys.bio:
Stephen M. Denenfeld has been associated with Lewis Reed & Allen P.C. or its predecessor since 1983. He attended the University of Michigan where he obtained a Bachelor's Degree in 1975, and was awarded his Juris Doctorate Degree from Wayne State University in 1978.

Although twenty-plus years of practice have given him experiences in several areas of law, Steve now focuses in the business and commercial arena, including commercial litigation, employment law, business torts, and general civil litigation. Steve also frequently serves as a mediator in both State and Federal Courts and has been certified as a facilitative mediator for the United States District Court for the Western District of Michigan.

Steve is a member of the State Bar of Michigan, the American Bar Association, is a past President of the Kalamazoo County Bar Association, and a past member of the Calhoun County Bar Association Executive Committee. Steve is admitted to practice before all State and Federal Courts in Michigan.

Steve's community activities are numerous and broad-ranging. He is a member of the Board of Directors and past President of the Kalamazoo Public Education Foundation, and the current Chairman of the Executive Committee and Advisory Committee for the Kalamazoo County LISC Housing Partnership. He is a past President of Living Ways, Inc. and past President of Living Ways Foundation, Inc. He is past Chairman of the Leadership Kalamazoo Advisory Board and the Community Development Act Advisory Committee to the Kalamazoo City Commission. Steve is a past Member of the Revenue Advisory Committee to the Kalamazoo City Commission and of the Kalamazoo City Commission Housing Task Force. He currently serves as a mediator for the Kalamazoo Community Dispute Resolution Center. Steve has also enjoyed coaching in the Oakwood and Milwood Little Leagues and Kalamazoo AYSO Soccer League.

attorneys.name: Maryanne J. Deneweth
attorneys.practice_type: Business & Commercial Law Lawyers in Clinton Township, MI
attorneys.bio:
Maryanne Deneweth graduated from L'Anse Creuse North High School in Macomb Township, Michigan and received a Bachelor of Science Degree from Michigan State University. Ms. Deneweth graduated from Thomas M. Cooley Law School in 1999, receiving a Juris Doctorate (with Distinction). While attending Cooley, she was a member of the Journal of Practical and Clinical Law and wrote for the Cooley Environmental Journal. She has acted as a legal research clerk for the Macomb Circuit Court, working for the Hon. John B. Bruff, and as a research clerk with the Michigan Department of Natural Resources. A State Bar of Michigan member since 2000, Ms. Deneweth is also a member of the Macomb County Bar Association. She has served as a Special Assistant Attorney General.

Ms. Deneweth has successfully drafted briefs and argued before the Michigan Court of Appeals and the Michigan Supreme Court. A lifelong resident of the State of Michigan, she is a member of the Real Property and Appellate Sections of the State Bar of Michigan, as well as a member of the Women Lawyers Association of Michigan and the American Agricultural Law Association.

Her primary practice areas include Business and Commercial matters, Zoning/Land Use, Eminent Domain and Municipal matters, as well as legal research, drafting and transactional matters.

attorneys.name: Samantha Smith Dickinson
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Westland, MI
attorneys.bio:
Samantha Smith Dickinson, Owner of The Smith Law Offices, graduated with Honors from Michigan State University with a Bachelor of Arts Degree in Psychology in 2005 and with a Juris Doctorate from Wayne State University Law in 2008.

Samantha began her legal career, while in law school, working with an esteemed Plaintiff’s Personal Injury attorney in Detroit, Jon Garrett. Jon was a mentor and asset to Samantha as she learned the practice of law.

Samantha opened The Smith Law Offices, PC in early 2010. She focuses primarily in Family Law, including Divorce and Child Custody. Samantha has tried a substantial number of cases in Wayne, Oakland and Washtenaw Counties with excellent results. Samantha also practices in the areas of Bankruptcy, Chapters 7 and 13, Criminal Defense and Plaintiff Personal Injury. Samantha has earned the esteemed ranking of Super Lawyer Rising Star 5 years in a row, along with a number of other awards and certifications.

When asked what she would like clients to know about her, Samantha replied as follows: “It has been immensely rewarding representing my clients with vigor since The Smith Law Offices opened in 2010. However, I believe that in the last few years I have had the opportunity to develop my practice and hone in on my expertise. Personally, in the last few years I have gotten divorced, remarried and have had to adjust to co-parenting my five (5) year old son with my ex-husband. My entire life dynamic has changed, and I now see firsthand what people are going through when they come in to see me to discuss filing for divorce or other child custody issues. I know that I am not doing anything perfectly in my own life, but I do hope learning my own life lessons and learning from all of my own friends, family, past clients and colleagues, that I have created a knowledge base that adds significant value for my clients when dealing with Family Law issues.”

Samantha lives in the City of Livonia with her husband, 5-year-old son, 12-year-old Chihuahua/Rat Terrier mix and is awaiting the arrival of her Border Collie puppy in early fall. When not at court or in the office, Samantha heads the Parent Action Committee at her son’s school, is actively involved in her son’s numerous extracurricular activities and enjoys spending time traveling, attending concerts and sporting events, playing golf, enjoying the outdoors and binge watching tv shows on Netflix. Samantha is an avid Michigan State and Detroit sports fan.

attorneys.name: Loren Dickstein
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Southfield, MI
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Dickstein received his Juris Doctor from Wayne State University Law School and a Bachelor of Business Administration from Western Michigan University. He practices law in all Michigan state-level district, circuit, and appellate courts, the United States District Courts for the Eastern and Western Districts of Michigan, and the United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit. He's handled major felony cases in courts throughout the United States. Before becoming a criminal defense attorney, Mr. Dickstein worked as a judicial and legal research clerk for multiple circuit court judges. His previous experience working as a clerk in the Circuit Court has given him invaluable insight into the inner workings of the criminal justice system and the ability to work with the courts to achieve the best possible outcomes for his clients.

As a trial attorney, Mr. Dickstein's practice focuses on felony and misdemeanor charges in both state and federal courts. Mr. Dickstein is passionate about defending the falsely accused and those mistreated by the authorities or the legal justice system. He has served as the lead trial attorney on numerous complex cases, and other lawyers hire him to assist in cases throughout Michigan. He has training from and courtroom experience with nationally prominent medical, psychological and scientific experts. Mr. Dickstein has obtained dismissals and ‘not guilty' verdicts throughout Michigan.

He frequently participates in continuing legal education to keep himself updated on the most current laws, techniques, areas of expertise, and court rulings that might affect his clients. Mr. Dickstein's professional memberships have included the State Bar of Michigan, Criminal Law Section, National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers, and Criminal Defense Attorneys of Michigan.

attorneys.name: Sandro DiMercurio
attorneys.practice_type: Business and Corporate Law Lawyers in Birmingham, MI
attorneys.bio:
Mr. DiMercurio practice focuses on Real Estate, Business and Corporate, Civil Litigation and Labor and Employment law. Mr. DiMercurio has jury trial experience on a variety of employment law issues, and recently played a large role in helping a client win a jury trial involving Family Medical Leave Act and Whistleblower Protection Act claims.Additionally, Mr. DiMercurio continues to conduct extensive research on unfair labor practice issues given the evolving nature of this area of law. Mr. DiMercurio also provides litigation and transactional support to clients on a variety of complex issues, including real estate matters, general commercial and contract disputes, and Uniform Commercial Code issues.

Mr. DiMercurio has assisted his clients with property acquisition, residential development, and property tax assessment appeals to the Michigan Tax Tribunal. Mr. DiMercurio has lectured and assisted in preparing for seminars to businesses and professional groups on emerging employment law issues, including the American Society of Employers and the Michigan Assisted Living Association.

Prior to joining Berry Moorman, Mr. DiMercurio served as an intern for the Macomb County Corporation Counsel. Then, Mr. DiMercurio worked as a law clerk for a business law firm in Troy, focusing his practice areas on Litigation, Business, and Real Estate.

Mr. DiMercurio is looking forward to further developing his involvement with the metropolitan Detroit community and local organizations.

attorneys.name: Senara R. Dollar
attorneys.practice_type: Litigation and Appeals Lawyers in Howell, MI
attorneys.bio:
Ms. Senara Dollar is an attorney who cares deeply about her clients and her community. Our legal system can be complicated and confusing and Senara is always ready and willing to help her clients navigate it with any issue they may be facing.

Whether as an individual or a large business, when you need a strong advocate, Senara is the attorney you want at your side. She concentrates her practice on civil and commercial litigation, real estate matters including land use and zoning issues, municipal law, as well as agricultural law and the Michigan Right to Farm Act. She also has experience in personal injury, construction litigation and general defense work.

Ms. Dollar graduated from Michigan State University College of Law. There she competed on the MSU Mock Trial Team and completed the Geoffrey Fieger Trial Practice Institute Certificate Program. She received her Bachelor of Science in Political Science and Paralegal studies at Northern Michigan University.

A proud veteran of the United States Air Force, Senara served six years in the Minnesota Air National Guard before pursuing her career in practicing law. While not at work, you can find Senara on her hobby farm riding her horses and spending time with her husband, Mason and their beloved Great Pyrenees, Bunker.

attorneys.name: Adam Dreher
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law Lawyers in Ann Arbor, MI
attorneys.bio:
Adam Dreher joined Nacht Law in 2025 after nearly a decade as a prosecutor. He was born and raised in Ypsilanti, but following the attacks on September 11, 2001, he enlisted in the United States Army and served as a Cavalry Scout with two combat tours to Iraq. Adam returned to Ypsilanti using the G.I. Bill to graduate from Eastern Michigan University and Michigan State University College of Law. At both schools, he began to hone his trial skills early by representing each school at mock trial and moot court competitions across the country. Before becoming a prosecutor, he interned in the appellate division of the Washtenaw County Prosecutor’s Office, where he gained valuable experience in Michigan’s appellate courts.

As a prosecutor, Adam worked hundreds of cases ranging from low-level misdemeanor offenses to complex international drug-trafficking prosecutions. He began his career in Ionia County, Michigan, where he prosecuted drunk driving offenses, assault and battery cases, and felony property crimes. Early in his career, Adam argued a case before the Michigan Supreme Court, a rare opportunity for a county prosecutor, which showcased his ability to master complex legal issues and advocate persuasively at the highest level of Michigan’s judiciary. Later, Adam joined the Wayne County Prosecutor’s Office, where he was assigned to prosecute homicide offenses and non-fatal shootings within the City of Detroit. The capstone of Adam’s career as a prosecutor was his appointment as an Assistant United States Attorney, where he prosecuted violent crime and drug trafficking offenses in Washington, D.C. At each level, Adam excelled in the courtroom.

Adam’s success in the courtroom is a direct result of his preparation outside of it. At Nacht Law, Adam’s practice focuses on employment law and criminal defense. Drawing on his extensive trial experience and investigative background, he provides clients with skilled, strategic representation in complex and high-stakes matters.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Grand Rapids, MI
attorneys.bio:
Stephen R. Drew is a founding partner of Drew, Cooper and Anding. He earned his undergraduate and law degree from the University of Michigan.

For over 43 years Mr. Drew has practiced in the areas of Civil Rights, Personal Injury, Sexual Harassment, Sexual Abuse, Police Misconduct, and Employment law, and has litigated complex cases in state and federal courts in Michigan and throughout the United States. Known for achieving exceptional results for clients on unpopular and challenging cases against large corporate defendants, he has gained the recognition and reputation as a fierce litigator.

Mr. Drew is a fellow in the American College of Trial Lawyers and the College of Labor and Employment Lawyers of the American Bar Association, where membership is selected based upon recognition of skill and professionalism. He has been named Super Lawyer in Michigan in the field of Personal Injury since 2007. He has also been awarded the Champion of Justice Award by the Michigan Bar Association and has been listed in the Bar Register of Preeminent Lawyers since 1997. Because of his skill and integrity, he is often sought by other lawyers to serve as a facilitator in lawsuits.

Mr. Drew was selected by his peers as the 2017 Best Lawyers “Lawyer of the Year” for Employment Law, Grand Rapids—a designation he has received each year since 2011.

attorneys.name: Myra S. Dutton
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Muskegon, MI
attorneys.bio:
For over 25 years, Myra Dutton has helped families and individuals navigate complex legal and educational systems. She has built her career as a dedicated education attorney and disability rights advocate, always focused on making sure her clients get the support they need.

Along the way, Myra has worked to improve communication between families and service providers. When those relationships become strained, she steps in to help rebuild trust and cooperation. Her goal is always to find solutions that serve the best interests of her clients.

She has successfully represented students in matters involving the IDEA, Section 504, and the ADA. From initial complaints to state or federal appeals, she walks with families through every step of the process.

In addition to litigation, Myra handles juvenile court matters, guardianships, and disability trusts. She enjoys tackling complex problems and brings a thoughtful, solution-focused mindset to every case she takes on.

Outside the courtroom, Myra provides education and training for parents, school staff, healthcare providers, and community advocates. She’s known for making legal topics accessible and empowering others to advocate effectively.

Earlier in her career, she served as a nonprofit CEO and higher education administrator. Even then, her primary focus remained advocacy and helping families find a path forward.

When she’s not working, Myra volunteers her time in the community. She also enjoys being outdoors and spending time with her three children and two grandchildren.

attorneys.name: Simon M. Edelstein
attorneys.practice_type: International Business and Trade Lawyers in Birmingham, MI
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Edelstein brings over twenty-eight years of experience in structuring and negotiating trade and investment transactions in Eastern Europe, where he represents U.S.-based clients across a broad spectrum of legal issues. His practice spans commercial, corporate, finance, tax, securities, antitrust, currency control, and labor law matters.

Mr. Edelstein guides clients through complex transactions such as acquisitions, joint ventures, and privatizations, ensuring compliance with local regulations and maximizing investment opportunities.

Additionally, Mr. Edelstein represents Eastern European and other international companies entering the U.S. market, advising them on corporate structure, regulatory compliance, and commercial operations. His immigration practice focuses on both corporate and individual clients, assisting with employment-based immigration matters for businesses, as well as family-based immigration for individuals, helping clients secure both temporary and permanent residency in the U.S.

Mr. Edelstein is fluent in Russian, Ukrainian, and Uzbek, allowing him to provide culturally informed counsel to his clients.

attorneys.practice_type: Liquor Licensing Lawyers in Troy, MI
attorneys.bio:
Scott D. Edwards had represented clients in general business and real estate matters for over 25 years. He has represented clients in connection with liquor licensing matters for over 15 years. His clients include national restaurant chains, independent restaurant operators, landlords, creditors, golf courses and hotels. As part of his practice, he has obtained every type of liquor license, prepared Asset Purchase and Stock Purchase Agreements, Buy-Sell and Shareholder Agreements, prepared and negotiated commercial contracts, including Management Agreements, Co-License Agreements and Option Agreements. He has represented creditors and debtors in the negotiation and preparation of security documents and loan transactions. He has represented Landlords and Tenants in lease negotiations and lease drafting as well as the sale and purchase of real estate. He is a liquor license contributor expert for the Institute of Continuing Legal Education for liquor licensing in Michigan, and he a contributor expert for liquor licensing matters for the Michigan Restaurant Association.

Mr. Edwards is a 1978 graduate of Oakland University, and he received his law degree from Wayne State University Law School and was admitted to the State Bar of Michigan in 1981.

attorneys.name: Laura E. Eisenberg
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Birmingham, MI
attorneys.bio:
Laura Eisenberg is a specialized family law attorney, with more than 30 years of experience handling divorce, custody, property settlement and related family law matters.

Laura has been recognized by numerous professional and legal organizations as a leading practitioner of family law. She has been designated as a "Michigan Super Lawyer" (top 5% of attorneys) as well as a DBusiness Magazine "Top Lawyer In Metro Detroit."

She is also a trained mediator and a presenter for the State Bar of Michigan Family Law Section's Family Law Forum, and the Oakland County Circuit Court's SMILE program. She is also currently the president of the Michigan chapter of the Academy of Matrimonial Lawyers.

Laura cares deeply about her clients, bringing her tireless energy and passion for the law to every case. She understands that when an individual is faced with a family law matter, he or she will have many important questions on their mind. She patiently and compassionately takes the time to help her clients understand all of their legal options, and to make sure that all of their concerns are addressed.

She uses her skill as a negotiator and as a litigator to fight for her client's rights from start to finish and has a reputation as an experienced and aggressive family law attorney who obtains exceptional results for her clients.

Laura prides herself on representing a diverse array of clients, including "everyday" men and women, as well as well-known area personalities and prominent local businesspeople. It speaks to Laura excellent reputation that many area attorneys have turned to her to represent them in their own personal divorces.

It is Laura's mission to stand beside her clients through every step of their legal proceeding, and to fight aggressively to ensure that every client obtains the best possible results and moves positively through the divorce experience.

attorneys.name: Lana M. Escamilla
attorneys.practice_type: Business Law Lawyers in Kalamazoo, MI
attorneys.bio:
Lana Maria Escamilla is a lifelong resident of Kalamazoo County, Michigan. She earned a Bachelor of Science, Cum Laude, from Western Michigan University in 2003, where she was a member of Lee Honors College and a McNair Scholar. She graduated from Michigan State University College of Law in 2007.

Lana has practiced in district, circuit and probate courts throughout the State of Michigan, as well as the Federal Bankruptcy Courts for the Eastern and Western District of Michigan. Her expertise is in bankruptcy and insolvency, workouts and collections with an emphasis on creditors’ rights. She has represented credit unions and banks throughout the United States. While clerking for Stephen L. Langeland, a United States Chapter 7 bankruptcy trustee and creditors’ rights attorney, she developed an interest in bankruptcy law. She continued on as an associate with his firm, until 2011, when she joined Capitol Bancorp Ltd., a holding company that held many bank charters throughout the United States as in-house corporate counsel. While employed as corporate counsel, she was part of the litigation team and the lead bankruptcy attorney.

Lana went back into private practice in 2014, was a founding member of Escamilla & Salisbury, PLLC and recently joined Lewis Reed & Allen, P.C. She continues to focus her practice on representing financial institutions with a focus on creditors’ rights, including bankruptcy, workouts and collections. Lana also represents individuals, non-profit organizations, and small businesses and has extensive experience in probate law, business transactions, including note sales, real estate law in the area of foreclosures, land contracts, landlord-tenant and civil litigation. She is on the rotation for the Kalamazoo County Probate Court to serve as guardian ad litem for vulnerable individuals in guardianship and conservatorship proceedings.

Lana is a member of the Kalamazoo County Bar Association (Member: Probate Section), State Bar of Michigan (Member: Business Law, Elder Law & Disability Rights, Litigation, Probate & Estate Planning, Real Property Law), Federal Bar Association of Western District of Michigan (Member: Bankruptcy Steering Committee, 2020- ), and American Bankruptcy Institute.

Lana has presented at Legal Aid’s “Probate & Pro Bono: Help Families Protect Assets & Achieve Homeownership Training Event” August 2022; Co-Authored “The Intersection of Bankruptcy and Probate Law” published in the FBA Bankruptcy Journal-Summer 2021 Issue; Spoke for the National Business Institute Collection Law Course June 2021; and Spoke at the 23rd Annual FBA Bankruptcy Conference 2011.

Lana enjoys being active in the community. She currently is a volunteer for the MCCE Mock Trial program. She has been instrumental in re-establishing the probate section of the Kalamazoo County Bar Association and is working with other community groups to establish legal clinics to assist underrepresented individuals. Some of her previous volunteer work includes serving on the City of Portage Parks and Recreation Board from 2017-2020 where she was instrumental in organizing the Great American Campout. She has raised funds and awareness for the Wilson’s Disease Association and petitioned the Detroit Marathon to add Wilson’s Disease Association as a charity in 2020. She coached girls on the run, volunteered at the pro bono legal clinic-civil, probate clinic, immigration clinics assisting refugees seeking asylum, and volunteering at the Gospel Mission.

When not working, Lana enjoys reading, drawing, hiking, dance and spending time with her family.

attorneys.bio:
Mr. Fagan is a recognized expert in the State of Michigan in the area of employment law, and civil rights litigation. He has many years of experience representing people who are victims of employment discrimination, sexual harassment, retaliation for engaging in whistleblowing activities, and mistreatment by the police. Mr. Fagan has achieved significant jury trial verdicts and million-dollar settlements on behalf of his clients.

Mr. Fagan is the Justice PAC Chair for the Michigan Association for Justice, and is also a member of its Executive Board and Executive Committee.

Mr. Fagan is a frequent lecturer at seminars through the Institute for Continuing Legal Education and the Michigan Association for Justice and has given presentations on topics including Trial Skills, Proving Damages in Employment Discrimination Cases, "Investigating the Egregious Harassment Case," "The Ultimate Trial Notebook for Employment Attorneys," and "The Ten Biggest Mistakes My Opponents Make."

Mr. Fagan is an appointed case evaluator for the Wayne County Circuit Court. He is a member of many professional organizations, including the Michigan Association for Justice and the National Employment Lawyers Association.

Mr. Fagan has a Preeminent "AV" rating by Martindale-Hubbell® (highest Peer Review Rating for Ethical Standards and Legal Ability).

Mr. Fagan has also been selected as a "Michigan Super Lawyer" by FindLaw since 2007 and has been selected for inclusion by his peers in "The Best Lawyers in America®" in the field of Labor and Employment Law since 2010 and was selected as one of the 2019 "Lawyers of the Year" award recipients in the field of Employment Law. He was also selected by DBusiness Magazine as one of the "Top Lawyers in Metro Detroit" in 2019 and has been selected for inclusion in "Leading Lawyers" since 2015.

attorneys.name: Brian J. Farrar
attorneys.practice_type: Employment Law For Employees and Employers Lawyers in Bloomfield Hills, MI
attorneys.bio:
Brian is an experienced trial attorney and the Managing Shareholder of the firm. He has successfully litigated numerous cases in federal and state courts involving wrongful termination, discrimination, unequal pay, breach of contract, wage and hour violations, and other civil rights matters. In addition to working with employees, Brian also represents several businesses by handling all of their employment law needs.

In March 2023, Brian obtained a nearly $3 Million verdict in federal court for an employee who was wrongfully terminated for reporting sexual harassment. In 2020, Brian negotiated a $1.46 Million pre-trial settlement on behalf of female college professors who alleged unequal pay and sex discrimination. This was one of the largest reported settlements for a gender discrimination case in the country. As lead trial counsel, Brian has also obtained many other large settlements and judgments for clients ranging from hourly workers to C-Suite level executives.

Many clients hire Brian to handle disputes over non-compete agreements. He is very familiar with how judges interpret these agreements, and frequently challenges the validity of non-competes in court. He also advises clients on all types of employment contracts, including severance agreements, and has drafted and negotiated compensation packages for corporate executives where millions of dollars are at stake.

Before joining Sterling Attorneys, Brian was a Senior Counsel for the City of New York Corporation Counsel’s Office. When he’s not practicing law, he serves his community as an Auxiliary Sergeant with the Birmingham Police Department, and graduated from the Oakland County Reserve Police Academy in 2018.

attorneys.name: Jeffrey H. Feldman
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Farmington Hills, MI
attorneys.bio:
Jeffrey H. Feldman is a well-known personal injury lawyer who focuses on electrocution cases across the United States. He has spent more than 35 years helping families whose lives were torn apart by electric shock and electrocution deaths.

Jeffrey has handled more electrocution cases than most injury lawyers in the country. He has also won several multi-million dollar verdicts and settlements for clients who lost loved ones in these tragic accidents.

What drives Jeffrey is making a real difference in his clients’ lives and helping prevent future injuries and deaths. He does this by uncovering the careless actions and bad decisions made by power companies and holding them responsible. His work sends a strong message to companies that put profits before safety. It also leads to new safety rules that help protect others.

Jeffrey’s success comes from his deep knowledge of law, engineering, and medicine. As a child, he was exposed to major medical advances. His father was a doctor who worked with Albert Sabin to help develop the polio vaccine. When Jeffrey chose to become a trial lawyer, he was drawn to complex cases that required strong medical understanding.

In his first electrocution case more than 30 years ago, Estate of Caroline Marie Bell v. Detroit Edison Company, Jeffrey represented the family of a 5-year-old girl who died after touching a downed power line hidden under leaves after a storm in rural Michigan.

The multi-million dollar verdict he won in that case led to a public safety campaign. A famous NBA player appeared in ads warning children to “Look up for power lines!”
