attorneys.name: Roger L. Myers
attorneys.practice_type: Complex Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Howell, MI
attorneys.bio:
ROGER L. MYERS concentrates his practice in complex commercial litigation and all real estate related matters, including zoning and land use, construction law, and property tax law.

Admitted to practice in Michigan and California, Mr. Myers is a member of both the State Bar of Michigan (and its Sections on Real Property Law, Business Law and Appellate Practice) and the State Bar of California. He is also a member of the Livingston County Bar Association.

Since 2007, Mr. Myers has been recognized each year as one of the Michigan SuperLawyers by Law & Politics Magazine. The SuperLawyers designation is an annual listing of the top 5% of attorneys in the state of Michigan as determined through a selection process based upon peer recognition and professional achievement. Mr. Myers is designated as one of the Michigan SuperLawyers in the practice areas of business litigation, real estate and zoning and land use law. As a result of his successful representation of clients in state and federal courts throughout Michigan, Mr. Myers was also selected in 2008 to become a Fellow in the Litigation Counsel of America, a trial lawyer honor society comprised of less than one-half of one percent of American lawyers. Fellowship in the Litigation Counsel of America is based upon an evaluation of the Fellow's accomplishments and ethical reputation as a trial lawyer.

Mr. Myers received a Bachelor of Arts from the University of Notre Dame in 1989 and a Juris Doctor, cum laude, from the University of Detroit School of Law in 1992, where he was the recipient of the 1992 Frank S. Sengstock Law Review Award and the 1992 Corporate and Environmental Law Chmielnicki Scholarship. While in law school, Mr. Myers was a member of the National Trial Team and the National Environmental Team. He was a Case and Comment Editor for the University of Detroit Law Review (1991-1992), From 1993 to 1994, Mr. Myers served as a law clerk to the Hon. Robert P. Griffin of the Michigan Supreme Court.

attorneys.name: Tracy N. Danner
attorneys.practice_type: Assessment Collection matters Lawyers in Plymouth, MI
attorneys.bio:
Tracy N. Danner-Bond is a partner with the Firm. She graduated from Michigan State University with Honors in 1993, where she obtained her Bachelor of Arts in General Business Administration-Prelaw and was a member of the Spartan Marching Band and Spartan Brass. Ms. Danner-Bond earned her Juris Doctorate from the University of Detroit Mercy School of Law in 1997, where she was the Managing Editor of the University of Detroit Mercy Law Review and a member of the American Inn of Court. Prior to joining the Firm in 2004, Ms. Danner-Bond practiced estate planning, probate, and tax law with a firm in downtown Ann Arbor.

In addition to being certified in probate and estate planning law by The Institute of Continuing Legal Education, Ms. DannerBond has extensive experience in Community Association Law. She handles assessment collection matters, lien foreclosure, bylaw enforcement, governing document amendments, as well as FHA certification issues. Ms. Danner-Bond has presented lectures on Community Association topics for United Condominium Owners of Michigan, the Michigan Chapter of the Condominium Association Institute, and the Firm's Condominium and HOA Board Education and Training (B.E.A.T.) program.

Ms. Danner-Bond has been licensed to practice law in Michigan since 1998 and is admitted to practice before the United States Federal District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan and the United States Tax Court. Ms. Danner-Bond served 8 years on the Board of Directors for her own condominium association in Canton, Michigan. This first-hand experience as a Co-owner and Director, in addition to being a Community Association Attorney, allows her to relate well to the many challenges that Community Association Boards face each day. Ms. Danner-Bond resides in Plymouth with her husband, two children, and their rescue dog. She has numerous interests, including spending time with family and friends, riding her Harley, reading (and listening to audio books), cooking, and traveling.

attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Clare, MI
attorneys.bio:
While finishing a Bachelor of Arts degree at Central Michigan University, Jay F. Trucks decided to go to law school. He earned his degree, Juris Doctor with Honors, from Detroit College of Law and moved to Clare, Michigan to set up practice amongst other Michigan attorneys.

In 1979, with two decades of general legal experience and a firm commitment to representing the common man, he focused his practice entirely on personal injury cases. Those who have worked with Jay are impressed by his honesty, integrity, and exceptional capabilities compared to other attorneys. Jay describes himself simply – as a straightforward person who works very hard for his clients.

For over ten years Jay served as Prosecuting Attorney. A member of Michigan Trial Lawyers Association and American Trial Lawyers Association, Jay currently practices with his son, Todd, in the firm Jay Trucks & Associates.

attorneys.bio:

He has more than 31 years' experience representing the injured and holds memberships in the Michigan Association for Justice and the American Association for Justice.

Although he becomes very involved in the difficulties of his clients, he enjoys his work because it is an opportunity to help them out of those difficulties. Todd is a skillful communicator. He gains the cooperation of the many people involved in his cases by always dealing with them in a professional manner.

attorneys.name: Mark Snover
attorneys.firm_name: The Law Firm of Hauer & Snover
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Bloomfield Hills, MI
attorneys.bio:
Mark Snover is a partner at the law firm of Hauer and Snover. His practice is devoted exclusively to family law. Mark specializes in litigating complex divorce cases, child support cases, as well as other cases dealing with family law issues. He represents men and women throughout Michigan.

Mark received his bachelors degree from University of Michigan and he received his law degree from University of Detroit Mercy School of Law. He has been selected as a Super Lawyer in the area of Family Law. Only 5% of attorneys in Michigan receive this distinction. Mark has been named to the Best Lawyers in America. He has been selected by his peers as a Leading Lawyer in family law. He was selected by the National Advocates, top 100 lawyers. He is a fellow of the Michigan State bar and the Oakland County bar foundation. Mark is listed in Martindale Hubbell's Bar Register of Preeminent Lawyers. He was also selected to the American Society of Legal Advocates, Top 100 Lawyers and the National Association of Distinguished Counsel's, Top One Percent.

Mark served on the State Bar of Michigan Family Law Council. He publishes a monthly article in the Michigan Family Law Journal. He has also authored other articles which have appeared in the Michigan Bar Journal.

Mark is an experienced litigator who will fight for his clients both in and out of the courtroom. He understands that his clients are experiencing the most difficult time in their lives. He is there to guide his clients every step of the way. While he always attempts negotiate a favorable settlement for his clients, he has significant trial experience and will not hesitate to take a case to trial if necessary to protect his client's interests.

attorneys.bio:

She also earned academic awards for the highest grade in several law school classes and top brief awards in appellate competitions, including a top brief award in a national criminal appellate competition.

Ms. Danner-Bond earned her Juris Doctorate from the University of Detroit Mercy School of Law in 1997, where she was the Managing Editor of the University of Detroit Mercy Law Review and a member of the American Inn of Court. Prior to joining the Firm in 2004, Ms. Danner-Bond practiced estate planning, probate, and tax law with a firm in downtown Ann Arbor.

In addition to being certified in probate and estate planning law by The Institute of Continuing Legal Education, Ms. DannerBond has extensive experience in Community Association Law. She handles assessment collection matters, lien foreclosure, bylaw enforcement, governing document amendments, as well as FHA certification issues. Ms. Danner-Bond has presented lectures on Community Association topics for United Condominium Owners of Michigan, the Michigan Chapter of the Condominium Association Institute, and the Firm's Condominium and HOA Board Education and Training (B.E.A.T.) program.

Ms. Danner-Bond has been licensed to practice law in Michigan since 1998 and is admitted to practice before the United States Federal District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan and the United States Tax Court. Ms. Danner-Bond served 8 years on the Board of Directors for her own condominium association in Canton, Michigan. This first-hand experience as a Co-owner and Director, in addition to being a Community Association Attorney, allows her to relate well to the many challenges that Community Association Boards face each day. Ms. Danner-Bond resides in Plymouth with her husband, two children, and their rescue dog. She has numerous interests, including spending time with family and friends, riding her Harley, reading (and listening to audio books), cooking, and traveling.

attorneys.bio:
David Nacht is at the peak of his career as a tenacious trial lawyer, strategist and negotiator. Nacht fights for people throughout their career, from student to employee to executive. Nacht is particularly proud of his efforts to expand due process rights for the accused: whether in the workplace, by federal investigators, or by prosecutors. Nacht’s approach is to listen to his client and put his client, and the client’s career and reputation first. The key: strategy and thinking several steps ahead. Fight for Dignity, but don’t let emotions cloud decision-making.

There are few lawyers that regularly practice both criminal and civil law in the federal and state courts. Nacht is one of them, and he uses what he learns in each sphere to improve his practice in the other.

Partner/Shareholder Disputes

A recent victory includes a settlement of over $800,000 for a small company shareholder and inventor for his shares in fourth quarter 2020.On April 6, 2022, David obtained complete dismissal of a lawsuit filed against his clients in a business partner dispute in Washtenaw County Circuit Court. The Court order went beyond dismissing the claims to also granting Nacht's clients the relief Nacht had sought - to obtain an accounting of the business.

University Proceedings

David Nacht recently won an important case in the Michigan Court of Appeals against the University of Michigan. The Court agreed with David that people bringing civil rights claims against the State of Michigan or its universities have one year to file their case, not just six months as the University argued. This decision is the first of its kind and is an important win for employees of the State and state universities who are seeking to protect their rights under the Elliott-Larsen Civil Rights Act.

In 2025, a police investigation of a Michigan nurse with representation from David resulted in no charges filed.

David Nacht obtained a denial of summary disposition in a disability civil rights act case against the University of Michigan for an employee with Crohn's disease. Nacht won on a hotly contested area of law: the effect of a prior different court's ruling in favor of the employer under a different legal theory. The case will now be set for trial.

In November 2023, David Nacht was local counsel for the Big 10 Conference in litigation with the University of Michigan and Coach Jim Harbaugh.

In August 2022, David Nacht persuaded a school district to withdraw its petition to expel a student for misconduct and convert it into a short-term suspension.

In 2020 and 2021 David achieved dismissal of claims in several university proceedings against numerous professors, staff and students in Title IX, academic misconduct and similar matters. Nacht is recognized as a leader in defending such claims and has done so successfully in Tennessee, Ohio, Massachusetts, and of course Michigan. Nacht’s most recent victory in January 2021 is for a university staff person accused by a peer and by a witness of an inappropriate touching. In 2020, Nacht also won internal proceedings for a professor facing the claims of multiple women alleging sexual misconduct; a physician accused of sex harassment against a coworker; a professor accused of inappropriate activity in the workplace among others.

In 2020, David successfully represented a globally prominent world-class university researcher against allegations of research misconduct. No publicity or harm occurred to the professor’s career in spite of a yearlong formal proceeding. This was Nacht’s third victory in a row for a tenured professor accused of academic misconduct.

In June 2020, David made new law for the rights of accused university professors in Carlock v Wayne State University.

Nacht has successfully represented hundreds of students accused of a variety of forms of misconduct against fellow students, against property, and of academic misconduct such as plagiarism or unauthorized collaboration.

Nacht previously represented a fraternity chapter sued by its national organization for allowing women and LGBT people to join.

Nacht represents many women and minority professors and staff facing discrimination.

Employment Law

United States Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit, Case No. 24-1098, Dwayne Seals v. Wayne County, MI, et al, filed February 25, 2025, David Nacht won an appeal challenging his victory at trial in a First Amendment retaliation case.

In 2023 Nacht, along with Amanda Ghannam, obtained a verdict of $180k plus attorney fees and costs in US District Court in Detroit in a first amendment retaliation case for a Wayne County employee whose pension had been terminated by the Retirement System after the client had objected to how his pension was calculated.

David Nacht successfully defended a social worker in a licensing dispute with LARA. The investigation was dismissed after an interview.

David prevailed in another LARA investigation. This case was for a Labor and Delivery RN and it was dismissed before formal investigation.

Employment Litigation and Negotiation

In 2023 Nacht along with Amanda Ghannam defeated a motion for summary judgment in an age discrimination case for a senior executive in US District Court in Fort Wayne Indiana.

In 2023 Nacht negotiated to preserve the state license of a public-school principal accused of misconduct with student grades. Nacht had previously negotiated his severance with his former employer in 2022 allowing him to find another position and advance his career.

In 2022, David Nacht brought a sex harassment lawsuit in Washtenaw County Circuit Court. The employer moved to dismiss the case based on documents they presented including a release and an arbitration clause with a shortened statute of limitations. The Court denied the motion relying on Nacht's arguments that factual questions about whether the documents were signed knowingly and voluntarily precluded an early victory for the employer.

In 2019-2020, David settled numerous employment lawsuits and negotiations totaling millions of dollars for his clients. A small portion of these cases required filing lawsuits in court. Most involved quiet negotiations that preserved privacy and reputation for his clients. Nacht routinely represents executives in health care, software, automotive, energy, manufacturing and finance industries. He negotiates for bonuses and options as well as severance, healthcare, references, and noncompete terms. Nacht also brings traditional age, race discrimination, disability discrimination and sex harassment lawsuits for employees at all levels in the workforce. He has numerous cases helping the careers of women of color, and people with chronic health conditions. Nacht has represented several young women in the restaurant industry who have been sexually harassed.

Severance Negotiations

Nacht negotiates multiple severance agreements every month.

In 2023, David Nacht represented an executive of a major privately held company in a severance negotiation. The executive was terminated before receiving most options he was scheduled to receive. Nacht negotiated for significant amounts of unvested options, more severance, and an innovative term for the Executive to not cash out immediately but to “ride out” the increase in share value prior to the company’s expected sale. The value of Nacht’s negotiation increased the benefit to the client a minimum of $500k with a likely return of over $1 million.

In 2022, David Nacht negotiated a pre-lawsuit severance settlement of $665K and a pre-lawsuit employment settlement of $300K.

David has negotiated and/or reviewed hundreds of severance agreements over the years. He has a strong understanding and successful track record of helping you understand what you are giving up in exchange for severance benefits and whether the amount of severance offered is fair compensation for what you are owed.

Noncompete Agreements and Trade Secrets

Nacht routinely counsels employees about noncompete agreements and has litigated many noncompete and trade secrets battles successfully. He has taught seminars to lawyers on the subject in both Michigan and Ohio.

Business Law Transactions

In 2021-2022, David Nacht

-negotiated the purchase of a technology company by executives of the company from the owner consortium.

-negotiated the sale of a fifty percent share of a restaurant amidst contract, tort and criminal allegations against his clients by the coowners;

-On behalf of a landlord, negotiated the removal of a wealthy tenant from a luxury home;

-negotiated the obtaining of unvested shares, stock options, and other long-term incentives for multiple executives in healthcare, medical devices, software, and tier one and tier two automotive suppliers.

Physicians/Health Care

Nacht obtained a probationary period of 1-180 days and then full restoration of a medical license for a client convicted of assault and battery.

Nacht won a grievance hearing for a physician whose job was non-renewed reversing the decision.

Nacht obtained a severance and terms of departure for a physician whose job was non-renewed allowing the client to obtain a new position at a higher salary.

Nacht negotiated to preserve the jobs of several physicians in 2022-23.

Nacht reviewed employment contracts for dozens of physicians in 2022-23.

In 2020, David successfully represented several physicians and nurses in license proceedings in Michigan and suspension of hospital privileges. Nacht represents physicians, nurses and other health care providers accused of misconduct or involved in business disputes. In fourth quarter 2020, Nacht successfully filed and settled a lawsuit by a radiologist against his former partner.

Nacht routinely counsels physicians on contracts and noncompete agreements as well as fraud investigations.

Criminal Defense

David Nacht has been frequently interviewed and quoted repeatedly in the Detroit News to offer legal commentary on the biggest criminal case in the state of Michigan. Jennifer and James Crumbley are both charged with four counts of involuntary manslaughter in connection with their son's killing of four students at Oxford High School in November 2021.

In 2023, Nacht obtained no jail time for a client convicted of unemployment system fraud in federal court in the Eastern District of Michigan.

In 2023, Nacht negotiated a plea in federal court in Detroit and obtained a sentence of under two years for a client facing guidelines of over ten years and a possible maximum of twenty years had he gone to trial in a fraud case.

In 2022, Nacht negotiated a plea and obtained a sentence of two years in a health care fraud case for a business owner facing ten years had he gone to trial.

In 2022, David and Fabiola Galguera obtained "Not Guilty" on a jury verdict in a felony criminal sexual conduct case in Washtenaw County, Michigan.

In 2020, David won the dismissal of a felony for a driver in an unfortunate accident with a pedestrian after a tenacious yearlong battle. Key to the defense was that Nacht performed his own investigation at the accident scene; interviewing neighboring home dwellers on his cell phone video on the evening he was hired.

In 2020, Nacht obtained a no-jail plea deal after defending a man in Ohio accused of first-degree criminal sexual conduct. Key to the defense was 1.) Nacht retained a medical expert who proved that the accuser’s account of being unconscious was not medically possible, and 2.) Nacht carefully reviewed the discovery material to recognize that there was an account by the victim that the prosecutor had not turned over. After obtaining those records, Nacht learned she lied to the investigator that she had been raped.

In other criminal work, Nacht is actively defending health care fraud claims against business owners and physicians in federal court in 2020-21.

Nacht also regularly defends criminal cases in federal and state court such as bribery, assault and battery, drug crimes, theft, and more.

Education Law

David Nacht represents families in manifestation determination hearings for students with IEPs or Section 504 status accused of misconduct.

University

In 2023., Nacht successfully represented a faculty member at a public university facing a federal criminal investigation and university investigation for a national security matter. No charges were brought, and the professor remains employed with the matter dropped.

In 2022, David Nacht successfully represented a whistleblower who raised concerns about abusive practices towards players and sexist behavior towards women employees at the University of Hockey Team. Following the investigation, the university changed its hockey leadership.

Other Disputes

David Nacht represented a commercial landlord in a dispute with a company that operated a short-term apartment rental service. The tenant company tried to overstay the lease trying to take advantage of pro-tenant eviction laws. Nacht deployed an aggressive strategy of posting notices and threatening to padlock on the grounds that the use of the apartments was not only in violation of the terms of the lease but also a violation of city ordinance. The tenant caved and moved out on time without the need for litigation.

In other regulatory work in 2020-21, Nacht currently represents an investor and consultant in an SEC investigation of a technology company.

Nacht represents principals and superintendents in license matters in Ohio and Michigan and in disputes with school districts. Nacht represents teachers when facing misconduct allegations.

Nacht routinely litigates property disputes involving contracts, zoning, driveways, and neighbor disputes.

Nacht holds degrees from Harvard and University of Michigan, where he was an editor of the Law Review. He has previously clerked for a federal judge and worked for Sen. John Glenn in Washington DC on Committee staff. Nacht formerly served as chair of the Ann Arbor Transportation Authority where he was instrumental in expanding service but maintaining fiscal stability. Nacht has served on numerous boards in non-profit organizations and local government. He continues to represent indigent criminal defendants in federal court and maintains a pro bono practice that includes a Methodist Church and Jewish Family Services, an organization that assists refugees and the elderly.

Nacht is licensed in Michigan, Ohio, and Massachusetts and works with local counsel in cases in other jurisdictions.

attorneys.name: Sarah Nasser
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Farmington Hills, MI
attorneys.bio:
Sarah Nasser is an associate attorney at Brown Borkowski & Morrow. Ms. Nasser was admitted to the Michigan Bar in 2023 and was a 2023 graduate of the University of Detroit Mercy School of Law, where she earned magna cum laude honors and graduated in the top 10% of her class. While in law school, Ms. Nasser was a junior member of the Law Review and a competitor in Moot Court. She received book awards in Contracts I, Professional Responsibility, and Access to Justice, and consistently earned Dean’s List recognition as a Dean Scholar. She earned her undergraduate degree from the University of Michigan–Dearborn, where she served as Student Government President.

Ms. Nasser was an active leader within the law school community, serving as Vice President of both the American Constitution Society and the Immigration Law Association. She also founded the Disability Law Association and served as its President. She worked as a teaching assistant for Torts and the Federal Pro Se Legal Assistance Clinic, where she provided guidance to unrepresented litigants in federal court.

Ms. Nasser gained practical legal experience through judicial externships with the Honorable Judge Linda V. Parker of the U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan and the Honorable Judge Berry of the Third Judicial Circuit Court of Michigan. Her article, “To Be Loved or To Be Healthy: A Disabled Individual’s Conundrum of Choosing Between Marrying Someone They Love or Continuing to Receive the Health Resources They Need,” was published in the UCLA Disability Law Journal.

Before joining Brown Borkowski & Morrow, Ms. Nasser worked as an associate attorney at McKeen & Associates, where she practiced medical malpractice law, and at Hewson & Van Hellemont, where she practiced Personal injury litigation.

attorneys.name: Nader W. Nassif
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Traverse City, MI
attorneys.bio:
Nader W. Nassif is a Michigan native and grew up in the Metro-Detroit area. He is a graduate of the University of Michigan, Dearborn where he earned a bachelor's degree in Economics and Thomas M. Cooley Law School where he earned his law degree. Nader was first licensed to practice law in 2009 and has gone on to successfully represent thousands of clients in both criminal and civil matters. Nader is a graduate of both the National Criminal Defense College (Mercer Law School), and the Criminal Defense Attorneys of Michigan (CDAM) Criminal Defense Trial College. He has worked in public service as a legal intern to the Judge Advocate General (JAG) of the Michigan National Guard, and as an attorney in both the Washtenaw County Public Defender Office and Model Cities Legal Services. Nader has also worked in private practice with multiple high-level criminal defense law firms representing clients in high-profile cases across the United States.

Nader became an attorney to use his problem-solving abilities to help people and has continued to expand his legal knowledge and practice since the beginning of his legal career. Nader has ghost written for several legal guides and law review articles and continues to be an active legal writer. He has had over 2,000,000 words of legal content published online on various legal websites. Nader's extensive legal experience, sharp attention to detail, and courage to take on the most difficult cases makes him the attorney you want in your corner.

attorneys.firm_name: Kevin P. Nelson - Tiffany & Bosco P.A.
attorneys.practice_type: Business Lawyers in Northville, MI
attorneys.bio:
Kevin P. Nelson | Shareholder

Tiffany & Bosco, P.A. Licensed in Arizona and Michigan

Kevin Nelson is a high-stakes commercial trial attorney with over 20 years of experience. Recognized for his ability to navigate "bet-the-company" litigation, Kevin acts as a proactive member of his clients' problem-solving teams. Since 2019, he has split his time between Michigan and Arizona, a transition that allowed him to master virtual practice ahead of the industry curve.

Core Practice Areas

Commercial & Business Litigation: Defending corporations and officers against multi-million dollar fraud and breach of contract claims.

Real Estate & Financial Services: Representing lenders and investors in everything from daily operations to complex quiet title and MDL class action defense.

Construction Law: Handling high-value transactions and litigation, including the termination and negotiation of AIA contracts.

Specialized Claims: Expertise in force majeure, insurance bad faith, and the enforcement of restrictive covenants.

Representative Successes

$1.5M+ Jury Verdict: Secured a judgment exceeding $1.5 million against a borrower and guarantors in February 2021 after defeating claims of fraud.

Complex Defense Victory: Successfully defended a commercial lender and its leadership against $10M+ claims of intentional interference and fraud.

MDL & Class Action Defense: Blocked class certification in federal court multi-district litigation related to consumer financial services.

Contractual Enforcement: Negotiated a $250,000+ settlement after an employee violated restrictive covenants, causing the employer to lose a business opportunity.

Project Recovery: Successfully terminated a contractor from a multi-million-dollar development and negotiated a new AIA contract to prevent project delays.

Appellate Success: Defended national lenders through the appeal process against a wide array of federal claims, including TILA, RESPA, FCRA, and the Fair Housing Act.

Professional Leadership & Recognition

AV Preeminent® Rated: Held the highest Martindale-Hubbell peer rating since 2014.

Best Lawyers in America: Recognized for Litigation – Construction (2023–2026).

Author & Educator: Revised and published Arizona Real Estate Law and Arizona Construction Law Annotated (Thomson Reuters) annually since 2013.

Community Impact: Former Board Member for the Boys and Girls Clubs of Greater Scottsdale and a founding donor for Arizona Autism United.

Personal

Beyond the courtroom, Kevin is a dedicated "sports dad," often traveling across North America and Europe for his daughter’s volleyball tournaments or his son’s hockey games. He is an avid, if self-deprecating, golfer and a supporter of youth sports.

attorneys.name: Kenneth F. Neuman
attorneys.practice_type: Complex Commercial Litigation Lawyers in Birmingham, MI
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Neuman has more than 31 years of experience in the courtroom and has obtained multiple verdicts and arbitration awards in excess of $1 million. Mr. Neuman has also successfully defended numerous claims brought against tier one and tier two automotive suppliers, builders and developers, and businesses of all types on a variety of commercial claims. In addition to his law degree, Mr. Neuman is a registered Certified Public Accountant and has a keen understanding of financial and business valuation, tax and accounting issues. Based on his experience, Mr. Neuman is appointed regularly as a Receiver over a variety of operating businesses in the automotive, real estate and health care industries by various judges in and around Michigan to assist the Courts in preserving business assets and/or to oversee an entity's orderly liquidation. Moreover, Mr. Neuman continues to be selected by numerous parties, and their counsel, as an arbitrator and/or facilitator on a variety of commercial disputes involving complex business and accounting issues. Mr. Neuman was also named a Best Lawyer, is a member of the State Bar of Michigan, Michigan Association of Certified Public Accountants, and as an Oakland County and Wayne Case Evaluation panelist. In addition, Mr. Neuman currently sits on the Board of Directors for the Home Builders Association, and is a Master on the American Inns of Court.

He has been named a Michigan Super Lawyer 10 consecutive years (including a Top 50 Business Lawyer and 1 of the Top 100 Lawyers for the entire State of Michigan), a Best Lawyer, and a dBusiness magazine Top Lawyer .

Mr. Neuman is also a registered Certified Public Accountant (CPA) and spent several years practicing with one of the “big eight” accounting firms, prior to beginning his legal career. He is a 1983 graduate of Michigan State University (B.A. in Accounting) and a 1986 graduate of the Wayne State University School of Law.

In addition to his role as client advocate, or in advising clients in countless commercial transactions over the years, Mr. Neuman has been called upon by Judges and fellow practitioners in Oakland, Wayne, Macomb, and St. Clair Counties to assist them as a receiver in complex commercial cases. Moreover, Mr. Neuman has served as an arbitrator and/or facilitator in numerous commercial cases involving areas of corporate law, real state, contracts, insurance, and business torts.

A frequent speaker at the continuing education seminars of the Michigan Association of Certified Public Accounts on litigation and expert witness related matters, he is also a current member of the Oakland County Bar Association (OCBA), State Bar of Michigan, Michigan Association of Certified Public Accountants, and American Association of Attorney-Certified Public Accountants.

In his spare time, Mr. Neuman has done volunteer work as a part of the OCBA Pro Bono Mentor Match Program, and currently serves as a Master in the American Inns of Court, providing guidance to new lawyers. He also volunteers his expertise for numerous nonprofit organizations in the metro Detroit area and is often called upon for his unique training in accounting and tax law by his peers looking for help in complex accounting and business cases.

Mr. Neuman resides in Oakland County with his wife of 25 years and 16-year-old basketballer son.

attorneys.name: C. Christopher Newberg
attorneys.practice_type: Civil Litigation Lawyers in Grand Rapids, MI
attorneys.bio:
Chris Newberg is an attorney at Kuiper Kraemer PC in Grand Rapids, Michigan. Chris helps individuals and businesses work through a wide range of legal issues, including pursuing and defending lawsuits, overseeing complex business transactions, drafting and reviewing contracts, and working through intellectual property and entertainment deals.

Chris represents both plaintiffs and defendants in a wide range of disputes throughout Michigan and beyond. He has considerable experience in the federal court system, representing clients in employment, intellectual property, insurance, and business cases. In the state court system, Chris helps clients with cases of all shapes and sizes, ranging from collections cases to insurance claims to partnership disputes to personal injury/wrongful death matters to cases involving allegations of fraud and theft. While much of his litigation experience comes from working on large, complex lawsuits, there is no case too big or too small for Chris.

From the courtroom to the boardroom, Chris works with Michigan businesses on a variety of formation, governance, compliance, employment, transactional, and related legal matters. He helps dozens of clients start and structure new businesses every year and frequently works with those same clients as their companies grow and evolve. Chris works very closely with the governing boards and executive staff of corporate clients on a wide range of various legal matters that come up in the course of business, ranging from ground level HR matters to multi-million-dollar mergers and acquisitions.

Chris is one of Michigan's few entertainment attorneys with actual, first-hand experience in the entertainment industry. Chris knows that to properly represent entertainers, you must not only know the law, but also the business. That's where he starts to separate from the pack. For over the past decade, Chris has traveled the country as the lead guitarist for Gunnar & the Grizzly Boys, which has given him invaluable perspective and experience concerning the operations of all sides of the music industry. At Kuiper Kraemer, he combines that experience with his experience in business planning and civil litigation to provide his clients with unparalleled insight and advice. Whether it's helping a new artist get started in business, working through complex intellectual property licensing issues, or negotiating publishing and record deals, Chris is more than qualified to help.

Chris grew up in Rockford, Michigan, and is now raising a family with his wife on the west side of Grand Rapids. He is a graduate and devoted fan of Michigan State University. After attending MSU, he received his law degree from the Thomas M. Cooley Law School. When he's not working, Chris enjoys playing music, playing with his rambunctious little boys, traveling, fishing, and enjoying the outdoors.

He helps dozens of clients start and structure new businesses every year and frequently works with those same clients as their companies grow and evolve. Chris works very closely with the governing boards and executive staff of corporate clients on a wide range of various legal matters that come up in the course of business, ranging from ground level HR matters to multi-million-dollar mergers and acquisitions.

Chris is one of Michigan's few entertainment attorneys with actual, first-hand experience in the entertainment industry. Chris knows that to properly represent entertainers, you must not only know the law, but also the business. That's where he starts to separate from the pack. For over the past decade, Chris has traveled the country as the lead guitarist for Gunnar & the Grizzly Boys, which has given him invaluable perspective and experience concerning the operations of all sides of the music industry. At Kuiper Kraemer, he combines that experience with his experience in business planning and civil litigation to provide his clients with unparalleled insight and advice. Whether it's helping a new artist get started in business, working through complex intellectual property licensing issues, or negotiating publishing and record deals, Chris is more than qualified to help.

Chris grew up in Rockford, Michigan, and is now raising a family with his wife on the west side of Grand Rapids. He is a graduate and devoted fan of Michigan State University. After attending MSU, he received his law degree from the Thomas M. Cooley Law School. When he's not working, Chris enjoys playing music, playing with his rambunctious little boys, traveling, fishing, and enjoying the outdoors.

attorneys.name: Michael A. Novara
attorneys.firm_name: Novara Tesija Catenacci McDonald & Baas PLLC
attorneys.practice_type: Employee Benefits Law Lawyers in Southfield, MI
attorneys.bio:
Background: Mr. Novara devotes his practice to the many facets of Employee Benefits Law. He represents numerous Fringe Benefit Funds in both the multiemployer (Taft-Hartley) industry and Public Sector. Mr. Novara counsels Pension and Health and Welfare Funds, as well as Vacation-Holiday, Supplemental Unemployment Benefits, and Joint Apprenticeship and Training Funds. He assists Funds with plan creation, design and compliance, along with plan mergers and terminations. He has navigated both self-insured and fully-insured Health and Welfare Plans through the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act ("PPACA"), and assists Defined Benefit Pension Funds through all aspects of compliance with the Pension Protection Act ("PPA"), and Multiemployer Pension Reform Act ("MPRA").

Mr. Novara has significant experience with the review of both traditional, and alternative, investment management agreements, and has also handled numerous Department of Labor ("DOL") and Internal Revenue Service ("IRS") audit/investigations. He routinely represents fringe benefit funds in collection matters, and has appeared before courts in Michigan and Illinois for cases involving the IRS, DOL, and Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

Education: Mr. Novara earned his Bachelor of Arts degree from Michigan State University in 2001 and his Juris Doctorate degree, Cum Laude, from Wayne State University Law School in 2004.

Professional Affiliations: In addition to the State and Federal Courts of Michigan, he is licensed to practice law in Nevada and Washington, D.C. as well. Mr. Novara is a member of the International Foundation of Employee Benefit Plans (IFEBP), the Michigan Association of Public Employee Retirement Systems (MAPERS), the American Bar Association (ABA), and the Macomb and Oakland County Bar Associations.

Speaking Engagements:

Speaker and Moderator: International Foundation of Employee Benefit Plans (IFEBP), April 2014 Health Care Management Conference, Orlando, FL. (Topic: HRA/HSA rules and the PPACA).

Speaker: International Foundation of Employee Benefit Plans (IFEBP) Webinar, June 2014 (Topic: HRA/HSA rules and the PPACA).

Speaker: Construction Association of Michigan (CAM) 2014 Annual Meeting & Trade Show, Detroit, MI (Topic: PPACA compliance, counting covered employees).

Speaker: Michigan Building and Construction Trades Council, 56th Legislative Conference. March 11, 2015, Lansing, MI (Topic: Updates on the MPRA and PPACA Cadillac Tax).

attorneys.name: Gary W. Novara
attorneys.firm_name: Novara Tesija Catenacci McDonald & Baas PLLC
attorneys.practice_type: Labor-Management Relations Lawyers in Southfield, MI
attorneys.bio: Mr. Novara is the firm's founder, and was one of the first attorneys in the State of Michigan to build a practice around the service of retirement systems with the passage of the Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA) in 1974. Mr. Novara has extensive experience in the employee benefits and labor arena, and has overseen countless rounds of labor negotiations, pension and fringe benefit plan mergers and dissolutions, as well as fringe benefit fund mergers. He also was the first to successfully complete the partition of an insolvent pension plan with the Pension Benefits and Guaranty Corporation (PBGC), the governmental entity that guaranties pension obligations of private employers. Additional areas of practice for Mr. Novara include Labor-Management Relations and Corporate Planning and Reorganizations. Mr. Novara earned his Bachelor of Arts degree Magna Cum Laude from the University of Detroit in 1970, and his Juris Doctorate degree from the University of Detroit in 1973, graduating Summa Cum Laude. Mr. Novara is a member of the International Foundation of Employee Benefit Plans (IFEBP), the American Arbitration Association (AAA), American Bar Association (ABA), and the Industrial Relations Research Organization. He is licensed to practice law in the various state and federal courts within the State of Michigan.

attorneys.name: Francie L. Novar
attorneys.practice_type: Family Lawyers in Ann Arbor, MI
attorneys.bio:
Since 2003 I have dedicated my law career to providing aggressive and honest legal representation in and around Washtenaw County. My law practice is devoted to representing individuals in matters involving: family law, with an emphasis on divorce, custody and support; probate & juvenile court matters; and general civil litigation, including guardianship disputes, breach of contract claims, intentional torts such as assault and battery, landlord-tenant, and mental health law. The philosophy of my office is to provide aggressive legal representation with unwavering honesty and integrity. Although most of my cases reach a settlement prior to trial, rest assured I will be prepared for trial should it be necessary. As required and when necessary, my office conducts extensive discovery prior to trial.

Prior to becoming an attorney I worked as an educator and administrator in the public schools for ten years and so I am able to draw from a variety of life experiences in order to better advise and assist my clients with their legal issues. I listen closely to my clients and together we map out the most appropriate course of action. In addition to Washtenaw County, I also have worked in Wayne, Jackson, Livingston and Oakland Counties.

attorneys.name: Paul F. Novak
attorneys.practice_type: Environmental Pollution Lawyers in Detroit, MI
attorneys.bio:
Paul Novak has a distinguished career of prosecuting complex civil cases against corporate wrongdoers and came to Weitz & Luxenberg to manage the firm’s Detroit office and continue his practice of fighting irresponsible corporate behavior.

In the late 1980s, as an Assistant Attorney General in Michigan Attorney General Frank Kelley’s office, Mr. Novak successfully attacked an illegal $1.5 billion transaction by Michigan’s largest public utility, Consumers Power Company, and saved hundreds of millions of dollars for Michigan’s ratepayers.

Mr. Novak is a national leader in litigation against the pharmaceutical industry. He led an $80 million case on behalf of all fifty State Attorneys General that attacked anticompetitive “pay for delay” deals that increase the price of prescription drugs and delay generic products from coming to market. And he has participated in several additional cases and obtained several hundred million dollars in recoveries on behalf of injured consumers and third-party payers who are overcharged by pharmaceutical companies.

Mr. Novak was appointed, by several state and federal courts, as lead counsel for plaintiffs in class action cases involving antitrust violations and in shareholder class actions. He has tried numerous antitrust and environmental enforcement cases to judgment and was awarded the Frank J. Kelley Distinguished Trial Advocacy Award for his service in the Michigan Attorney General’s office. His antitrust work has been featured in the National Law Journal on the “Plaintiff’s Hot List”. He is routinely recognized as one of Michigan’s Super Lawyers, as a Best Lawyer in DBusiness Magazine, as AV-rated by Martindale Hubbell, and as one of the top plaintiff antitrust lawyers in the nation by the Global Competition Review’s Who’s Who in International Competition Law. He was the former division head of the Special Litigation Division in the Michigan Attorney General’s office with responsibility for all antitrust, securities regulation, and utility ratepayer consumer advocacy matters. And he served as the City Attorney of Lansing.

He sits on the State Bar of Michigan’s U.S. Courts Committee. Among dozens of legal and civic organizations, Mr. Novak served as a member of the:

State Bar of Michigan’s Antitrust, Franchising and Trade Regulation Section (former chair)

National Association of Attorneys General Midwest Antitrust Enforcement Task Force (former chair)

National Association of Attorneys General Prescription Drug Pricing Task Force

Michigan Attorney General’s Litigation Advisory Board

Lansing City Council

Lansing Economic Development Corporation

He clerked at the Federal Trade Commission Regional Office in Atlanta, Georgia, the Michigan Public Service Commission in Lansing, Michigan, and as a Lyndon Baines Johnson Congressional intern while working on Capitol Hill in Washington D.C.

attorneys.name: Karl P. Numinen
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Law Lawyers in Marquette, MI
attorneys.bio:
Mr. Numinen is a trial lawyer and senior partner of the firm Numinen, DeForge & Toutant, PC., in Marquette, Michigan. His practice has focused on criminal defense and courtroom litigation for over 30 years. He is a fellow in the American College of Trial Lawyers and has been recognized as one of Michigan's top lawyers by Best Lawyers in America®, Super Lawyers® and Leading Lawyers® magazine. Mr. Numinen is recognized as a Preeminent Attorney with an "AV Rating" by Martindale-Hubbell. He is a past President of the Criminal Defense Attorneys of Michigan (CDAM) and has served on its Board of Directors for many years. He is also a member of the National Association of Criminal Defense Lawyers (NACDL). He currently serves as a member of the State Bar of Michigan Representative Assembly.

Mr. Numinen has tried cases in numerous state and federal courts, obtaining acquittals on virtually every kind of criminal case, including murder, sexual assault, drugs, tax evasion, child abuse, robbery, and drunk driving. He has also obtained multimillion dollar verdicts and settlements for clients, including a top ten verdict in Michigan, as recognized by the Michigan Lawyers Weekly. He has appeared in special episodes of "Dateline NBC", A&E's "Accused: Guilty or Innocent?", and "Fatal Vows." Coverage of his trials and cases have appeared in The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal, the Detroit Free Press, Michigan Lawyers Weekly, and the Michigan Bar Journal. He was also featured in a profile in Leading Lawyers magazine.

In addition to his trial work, Mr. Numinen has a record of successful appellate cases in the Michigan Court of Appeals, Michigan Supreme Court, and the Sixth Circuit of the United States Court of Appeals. His published appellate opinions include victories representing adoptive parents in a step-parent adoption case, a former state employee's claims for non-duty disability retirement benefits, and defending a client against her former boyfriend's claims to her real estate and other property rights.

Mr. Numinen has extensive experience as an instructor in trial skills advocacy. He has taught on the faculty of the prestigious Hillman Trial Advocacy Program of the Federal Bar Association of the Western District of Michigan as well as the CDAM Trial College and Evidence Boot Camp. He created the CDAM MasterClass program and has taught numerous seminars, including classes on the cross examination of snitches, handling false confession cases, preparing your client to testify, the use of experts, and effective voir dire. He has also presented many webinars on criminal law issues for CDAM and NACDL. He wrote two monographs published by the Institute for Continuing Legal Education on "How to Challenge a Search Warrant of a Home" and "How to Prepare a Client to Take the Stand in a Criminal Case."

attorneys.name: Bart Paul O'Neill
attorneys.practice_type: Medical Malpractice litigation - Plaintiff Lawyers in Detroit, MI
attorneys.bio:
“I represented doctors, hospitals and insurance companies for 15 years with a heavy heart for the patients and their families that were so often my adversaries. After watching and being appalled at how the insurance side works in some instances in 2017, I began representing victims of medical malpractice and their families. It was the best professional decision I have ever made, and bringing my unique defense background to the patient’s side has been an asset for my clients.”

Bart Paul O’Neill has more than 22 years of experience as a litigator, starting his law career representing physicians, hospitals and insurance companies. This defense background has given him a unique perspective representing victims of medical malpractice and personal injury.

O’Neill joined McKeen & Associates in 2022. He graduated from the University of Detroit Mercy with a bachelor’s degree in political science and certification in business administration. He is a graduate of Wayne State University law school. He is a member of the State Bar of Michigan and the Michigan Association for Justice.

When O’Neill is not practicing law, he spends time with his children, exercising and enjoys sports, writing and music.

He earned B.A. in Political Science with a Certificate in Business Administration from the University of Detroit Mercy in 1998; Juris Doctorate Degree from Wayne State University in December of 2001.

attorneys.name: Ann O’Connell
attorneys.practice_type: Business and Corporate Law Lawyers in Birmingham, MI
attorneys.bio:
Ann O’Connell is a tax attorney with extensive experience representing clients in complex tax matters. She advises individuals, businesses, and nonprofit organizations on tax controversy issues, tax planning, and compliance with federal and state tax regulations.

Ms. O’Connell represents clients before the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) and the Michigan Department of Treasury, as well as in proceedings before the United States Tax Court, Michigan Tax Tribunal, and Michigan Court of Appeals. Her practice focuses on a broad range of tax-related matters, including qualified retirement plans, non-qualified deferred compensation plans, welfare benefit plans, tax reporting and withholding issues, and Department of Labor compliance. She also provides strategic counsel on Employee Retirement Income Security Act (ERISA) matters and corporate tax planning.

Before joining Berry Moorman, Ms. O’Connell worked at Ernst & Young, LLP and Rubenstein Isaacs, P.C., where she gained significant experience handling complex tax issues for a diverse range of clients.

attorneys.name: Phil Paras
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Birmingham, MI
attorneys.bio:
Phil Paras was born and raised on the outskirts of Chicago in Northwest Indiana. He is now proud to call Michigan his home.

Phil attended Indiana University for his undergraduate and received his Juris Doctorate from Northern Illinois University School of Law in 2020. While in law school, he participated in Moot Court and the Trial Competition. During law school, Phil was also employed as a student attorney in the Health Advocacy clinic where he assisted injured and sick victims with their legal needs.

Upon graduating law school, Phil received admission to practice law in Massachusetts and Illinois. In Boston, he found himself trying criminal defense and personal injury cases. Family disputes, business litigation and civil rights claims were his main areas of focus.

Phil returned to the Midwest in 2022 and was immediately admitted to practice law in Michigan. Since being admitted to practice in Michigan, Phil has solely focused his practice on personal injury cases. He has handled countless of cases that include motor vehicle accidents, slip/trip and falls, and general negligence. He takes great pride in helping injured victims with their legal needs in Michigan, and continues to do so for Scott Goodwin Law P.C.

When Phil is not fighting for his clients, he enjoys spending time with his family, golfing, and time outside.

attorneys.name: Michael Patrick Parillo
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Grand Blanc, MI
attorneys.bio:
A partner with the firm, Mike Parillo concentrates in personal injury litigation, representing individuals and families who have been harmed as the result of the negligence of others.

For more than 17 years, Mike has appeared in courtrooms across Michigan in cases involving first- and third-party automobile and motorcycle accidents, dog bites, premises liability, and wrongful death claims, securing numerous six- and seven-figure verdicts and settlements.

Along with his commitment to his clients, Mike gives back to his profession in a number of ways. He has served on the Board of Directors of the Genesee County Bar Association since 2008, and is the outgoing President of the Flint Trial Lawyers Association. Mike also serves on the Board of the Michigan Association for Justice.

Mike is a lifelong resident of Flint and is very active in the Genesee County community. He is a member of St. Pius X Catholic Church in Flint, where he also coaches his son in youth sports. Mike is also a member of the Downtown Flint Optimist Club and will serve as President of the Flint Golf Club in the fall of 2014.

Mike earned Bachelor of Arts degrees in English and History from Michigan State University. He earned his Juris Doctor from the Pettit College of Law at Ohio Northern University in Ada, Ohio.

attorneys.name: Ryan Paree
attorneys.practice_type: Employment and Labor Law Lawyers in Detroit, MI
attorneys.bio:
Ryan Paree has known his entire life that he was going to be an attorney who used his skills to help those in need. He graduated from Albion College in 2010 with degrees in English and Philosophy and from Wayne State University Law School in 2013. While at Wayne Law, Ryan was an Article Editor and Board Member of the Journal of Law in Society, which published his paper in 2013. Additionally, he held two positions, Director of Student Affairs and Student Board of Governors Representative with the American Pacific American Law Student Association.

Since graduating law school, Ryan has worked in several areas of law, including construction, collections, insurance, and bankruptcy. While he had a knack for collections, Ryan felt strongly that his law license should be used for good and he began working with those in need to protect them from the corporations that looked to take advantage of them. Prior to working at Miller Cohen, Ryan did this primarily by fighting against debt collectors, cancelling out garnishments, and stopping foreclosures by assisting people in filing for bankruptcy. At Miller Cohen, Ryan puts his passion to good use in the areas of Employment and Labor law.

attorneys.name: Raymond J. Pater
attorneys.practice_type: Divorce Lawyers in Holland, MI
attorneys.bio:
Raymond Pater was born in The Netherlands as one of eight children. After his family immigrated to the US, and although of modest means, six of his siblings attended college and two went on to obtain PhDs, later becoming college professors. An older sister never attended high school, but was admitted to college because of a nearly illegible transcript and ironically went on to become a high school teacher.

While attending grade school and high school, he worked in the family business selling eggs and chickens on the streets of South side Chicago. After graduating from high school he worked in a steel mill in East Chicago, Indiana. That experience convinced him to change course and he attended Indiana University, Calvin College and Grand Valley. After graduation he worked in sales, then taught school, and then attended law school.

Ray graduated Magna Cum Laude from law school in 1983, one day after his youngest daughter was born. He started in general practice as a solo practitioner, then went to work for a leading collection law firm, and in 1990 began working in Holland, Michigan, with Coupe & VanAllsburg; that became Coupe, VanAllsburg & Pater; and finally Coupe Pater, PC. He has been in solo practice since 2006.

Ray has been involved as a Big Brother, deacon in his church, school board president, and has served as a mentor at Guiding Light Missions in Grand Rapids.

Ray and his wife of 35 years, Marcia, have three children: a businessman in Grand Rapids, an attorney in Manhattan, and a teacher in Denver (who claims to be his favorite child).

His practice includes family law, collections, contracts and contract litigation. He has practiced in courts over much of the State of Michigan, now working primarily in Ottawa and Allegan Counties. Assisting in the office are Heather Prince and Judy Tiemeyer.

Lawyers were formerly called Attorneys & Counselors at Law. Ray attempts to fulfill the tradition when attorneys knew their clients well and could counsel them to avoid or minimize the costs and travails often associated with the legal system.

attorneys.name: Randall A. Pentiuk
attorneys.practice_type: Cooperative Law Lawyers in Wyandotte, MI
attorneys.bio:
Randall (Randy) Pentiuk is an attorney who specializes in representing municipalities and public corporations, housing cooperative law, non-profit entities, and business clients. Randy represents dozens of housing cooperatives throughout Michigan and Illinois and provides legal consulting for local counsel to many more housing cooperatives throughout the United States. He also serves as legal counsel to several Michigan municipalities in Metropolitan Detroit and surrounding areas.

Since 1985, Randy has been involved in all aspects of representing housing cooperatives, providing services spanning the full spectrum of the legal affairs of housing cooperatives. These services range from researching and drafting legal opinions and rules, representation in all courts and tribunals, preparing and reviewing contracts, employment and personnel matters. Additionally, he advises housing cooperative Boards in such matters as HUD and State Housing Authorities, drafting amendments to cooperative governing documents as well as mortgage refinance and share loan issues.

Mr. Pentiuk is also strongly committed to the ideals of supporting the local community through successful municipal governance, and in this regard proudly serves as legal counsel to the cities of Riverview, Gibraltar, Allen Park, the Charter Township of Royal Oak and serves as special counsel to the City of Taylor. Randy provides legal counsel on various matters, including labor issues, contracts, general litigation, real estate, and election and governance procedure. Randy oversees the prosecutions for the cities of Riverview, Allen Park, Gibraltar, Charter Township of Royal Oak and Wyandotte.

Prior to starting out, Randy worked as a Research Attorney for the Michigan Court of Appeals in 1981. After serving at the Court of Appeals, he entered private practice and formed Pentiuk, Couvreur & Kobiljak, P.C. in 1989. Over thirty years later, Pentiuk, Couvreur & Kobiljak has now established itself as the premier housing cooperative law firm in the Midwest region. This feat is in large part attributed to Randy’s dedication to the specialized practice of housing cooperative law. He created the National Cooperative Law Center where he and his team of cooperative attorneys publish regularly. He has written numerous articles on the subject of housing cooperative as well as three primers geared specifically to housing cooperatives including the Cooperative Housing Law Primer, 101 Ways to Improve Your Cooperative, and A Primer for New Cooperative Board Members. Randy also regularly publishes legal articles to both the MAHC Messenger and the National Association of Housing Cooperatives.

In 1981, he was elected to the Board of Directors of the Detroit Rescue Mission Ministries, an inner city ministry employing over 200 staff with a budget of over $21 million, and continues to serve as its Chairman.

attorneys.name: Angela B. Peterson
attorneys.practice_type: Criminal Defense Lawyers in Southfield, MI
attorneys.bio:
Angela B. Peterson is a veteran criminal defense lawyer who dedicated her career to the zealous and passionate defense of clients charged with felony and misdemeanor charges in state and federal court.

Ms. Peterson received her Bachelor of Communication Arts from Wayne State University and her Juris Doctor from Wayne State University Law School. She was a Merit Scholar at WSU. She is admitted to practice law in all Michigan state courts and the United States District Court for the Eastern District of Michigan.

As a lifelong musician, entertainment law initially piqued Ms. Peterson’s interest and became the starting point of her career. Her desire to help people caused an expansion of her practice to include family law. It wasn’t long after that that her innate abilities as an advocate and keen sensibility for the facts and ensuring that the rights of people are not violated, quickly led her toward criminal defense. She has now enjoyed a successful 15 years defending criminal charges, with an impressive acquittal rate that has earned the respect of countless judges and prosecutors. The respect she has earned due to her continuous and exemplary results allows her to handle felony and misdemeanor cases from a power position.

She is active in public service and community outreach. Although her focus today is on providing exemplary retained criminal defense practice, she proudly dedicated several years sharpening her litigation skills while providing public defense in Wayne and Oakland counties. She’s tried many capital cases (including homicide and criminal sexual conduct), and her ability to persuade a jury is highly renowned. She maintains a great rapport with the bench and bar as a vigilant defender and consummate professional, affording her clients the benefit of zealous and effective negotiations when necessary.

Ms. Peterson’s passion, professional relationships, and experiences have distinguished her as an attorney known for her prowess in and out of the courtroom. She has earned a reputation as fearless and tenacious in fighting for the best results for her clients.

Ms. Peterson participates in continuing legal education, and her professional memberships include the State Bar of Michigan (Criminal Law and ACES sections) and the Wayne County Criminal Defense Bar Association.

attorneys.name: Vincent R. Petrucelli
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Iron River, MI
attorneys.bio:
Vincent R. Petrucelli is a trial lawyer with over 49 years of experience in trying all types of personal injury and wrongful death cases. He founded the law firm in 1979 with his wife, Nora A. Petrucelli.

Mr. Petrucelli received his Bachelor of Arts degree in 1971 from the University of South Dakota and his law degree from Hamline University School of Law in 1976. He is licensed to practice law in Michigan and Wisconsin and is admitted to practice before all Michigan and Wisconsin State and Federal Courts.

Over his career of 47 years, Mr. Petrucelli has obtained multi-million dollar verdicts and settlements for his clients. He has taught trial practice techniques and the use of technology in litigation as a faculty member of the Northern Michigan Trial Skills Workshop, the Michigan Institute of Continuing Education, the Michigan Association for Justice and the Wisconsin Bar Association.

He is a fellow in the American College of Trial Lawyers (limited to 1% of the trial lawyers in each State), a Diplomat in the American Board of Trial Advocates, a Michigan Super Lawyer and has attained an AV rating, the highest level award for professional excellence, from the Martindale-Hubbell Law Directory.

attorneys.practice_type: Estate Planning Lawyers in Troy, MI
attorneys.bio:
Sharri L. Rolland Phillips, Esq. holds a Bachelor of Arts in Economics from Oakland University and a Juris Doctor from the Detroit College of Law (Michigan State University College of Law). She holds a Certificate of Completion in the areas of probate and estate planning issued by the Institute of Continuing Legal Education and the Probate and Estate Planning Section of the State Bar of Michigan. She has a broad background in Alternative Dispute Resolution and is a trained general civil mediator.

Ms. Phillips founded her firm with a focus on Probate & Estate Planning. Her mission is to insure justice and help clients position their assets as intended. To that end, she draws upon her experience in agriculture, land stewardship/development, industry, and closely held small business. She practices in Oakland, Macomb, and Lapeer Counties and currently serves the Probate Court in Guardianship, Conservatorship and Mental Health proceedings.

Ms. Phillips is a member in good standing of the State Bar of Michigan; Oakland County Bar Association, and Lapeer County Bar Association. She is a past President of the D. Augustus Straker Bar Association; a recipient of the National Bar Association's Outstanding Chapter Award - Region VI (Kentucky, Ohio, Michigan, and Tennessee); a past Treasurer of the National Bar Association - Region VI; and past Director of the D. Augustus Straker Bar Foundation.

At MSU Law, Mr. Phillips was an editor for the Journal of Medicine and Law, where his article discussing federal preemption of state law failure to warn claims as related to Pharmaceuticals, was selected for publication.

Mr. Phillips has experience with auto negligence, no-fault (including provisions unique to the Michigan Assigned Claims Plan), construction law, real property law, and general commercial litigation.

Mr. Phillips is licensed to practice law in Michigan.

attorneys.name: Ryan Piekarski
attorneys.practice_type: Personal Injury Lawyers in Southfield, MI
attorneys.bio:
Ryan has been with Moss & Colella, P.C. since 2010. In his role as the senior litigation attorney with the firm, he is responsible for handling cases from the moment clients walk in the door until the time their case is completed. He handles the investigation and management of clients’ claims, discovery matters, court hearings, negotiation of settlements, and, of course, trials. He has argued in courts all over the State of Michigan, from local districts up to the federal level. He has also handled successful briefings and arguments in the Michigan Court of Appeals. Although he has performed work on all types of civil litigation, his specialty are cases involving personal injury, including automobile no-fault and negligence, premises liability, and medical malpractice. It is his passion to help clients who have been injured through no fault of their own, yet are often bullied and re-victimized by insurance carriers and corporations who are too stubborn or callous to pay what they owe.

Ryan believes that communication is fundamental to the relationship between an attorney and his client. Despite what many think, most people he meets with have never been injured in an accident or been involved in any kind of litigation. That is why, even from the very first conversation with a potential client, he believes it is important to provide education about the law and to answer any questions they have about their case. This open line of dialogue is encouraged at every point along the way so that a client never has to navigate this process on their own.

Although he grew up in Michigan, Ryan completed his undergraduate and law degrees at Loyola University Chicago. Since returning to Michigan to practice law, he has been a member of the American Bar Association, the Michigan Bar Association, and the Oakland County Bar Association, as well as the Michigan Association for Justice. Since 2019, he has been selected by the National Trial Lawyers as a Top 40 Under 40, and in 2021 was named in the group’s Top 100. Despite these honors from peers, his most rewarding achievement is the knowledge that he has been able to help a client achieve a result to their case that is just, fair, and valuable.

Jeffrey L. Pietsch joined Anselmi Mierzejewski Ruth & Sowle P.C. as an associate attorney in 2019, responsible for handling first- and third-party no-fault litigation defense.

Mr. Pietsch earned his Bachelor of Arts degree from the University of Michigan-Dearborn in 2007, graduating with distinction, and obtained his Juris Doctorate from Wayne State University in 2010.

Virtually all of Mr. Pietsch’s legal career has been in the area of no-fault and auto negligence. Prior to becoming an attorney, Mr. Pietsch worked as a law clerk at a plaintiff’s personal injury firm that specialized in third party no-fault litigation on behalf of significantly injured victims of automobile negligence. After obtaining his law license, Mr. Pietsch spent over seven years representing plaintiffs in various stages of first- and third-party no-fault litigation, including pre-litigation negotiation and settlement matters.

Mr. Pietsch is licensed to practice law in Michigan.

attorneys.name: Jacob Porcarelli
attorneys.practice_type: Lawyers in Detroit, MI
attorneys.bio:
As a proud labor and employment lawyer, Jacob did not end up in this field by accident. Jacob understands that employees often face unfair and illegal treatment while at work and the difficulties associated with that. Whether it be a union issue or an issue of discrimination, Jacob is passionate about fighting for the rights of his clients. Jacob’s passion is informed by his personal ties to organized labor and belief that discrimination has zero place in our society.

Jacob attended Miami University in Oxford, Ohio, on an academic scholarship, where he graduated with a degree in Political Science. At Miami, Jacob was a member of many organizations and was nominated to serve on two student-led boards.

He subsequently graduated Cum Laude from the University of Toledo College of Law in 2023, after attending school full-time and working part-time. During law school, Jacob worked at a local criminal defense firm where he assisted with expungements, driver’s license restorations, and trials. He also spent time as a clerk for the Hon. Daniel S. White of the Monroe County Circuit Court handling civil and business court matters. In addition to working and attending class, Jacob served as the Vice President of Toledo Law’s Labor and Employment Law Association.

Prior to joining the team at Miller Cohen, Jacob worked at a plaintiff’s firm in Detroit, where he represented clients in employment discrimination, personal injury, and civil rights cases.

attorneys.name: Marie A. Pulte
attorneys.practice_type: Family Law Lawyers in Plymouth, MI
attorneys.bio:
I am a family law attorney, mediator, Collaborative practitioner and arbitrator practicing primarily in Oakland, Livingston, Washtenaw, and Wayne counties since 1987. I am a trained Collaborative Divorce attorney and a past board member of the Collaborative Practice Institute of Michigan, (CPIM). I am also a past chair of the Family Mediation Council - Michigan, and Wayne County Chapter of the Family Mediation Council - Michigan.

My philosophy is to assist parties in getting through the family law arena as amicably as possible whether acting as an advocate for one party or a neutral for both parties. I believe that alternative dispute resolution options should be utilized whenever possible.

I have coached at various domestic mediation trainings, presented at family law, mediation and domestic violence seminars, served on the Mediation Advisory Board for the Institute of Continuing Legal Education, and provided volunteer services to various other organizations related to family law. I am married to attorney Carlo Martina and have four wonderful children.

attorneys.name: Kelly J. McNerney Quardokus
attorneys.practice_type: Elder Law Lawyers in Portage, MI
attorneys.bio:
Kelly J. McNerney Quardokus is the principal attorney and owner of the firm and has been practicing in the area of elder law for nearly two decades in both a large and small firm environment. Before entering private practice, Ms. Quardokus spent more than 14 years working for several statewide nonprofit organizations such as the Michigan State Bar Foundation, Michigan Office of the State Long Term Care Ombudsman, State Bar of Michigan, and Western Michigan Legal Services. She continues to remain active statewide and locally to advocate for vulnerable populations, especially seniors and people with disabilities. Ms. Quardokus is active in the State Bar’s Elder Law and Disability Rights Section, serving as previous chair of the Section and past chair of the Legislative Committee for several years. She is also a member of the National Academy of Elder Law Attorneys and a Supporting Fellow of the Michigan State Bar Foundation. Ms. Quardokus serves as chair of the Older Adult Services Advisory Council for Kalamazoo County and is on the governing board for Lending Hands of Michigan Inc.

Although born and raised in Southwest Michigan, Kelly (Niles) and husband, John (Bridgman), loved Kalamazoo and made it home after Bronco Days at Western Michigan University. Kelly and John have two “above average” children, Amelia and Alex Quardokus, with whom they enjoy spending time, even though the kids are adults and no longer “have to.” Kelly enjoys co-ed softball (although she is now retired), family volleyball, reading, thrifting and vintage shopping, nature trail walks with the family dog, and teaching Sunday School at Immanuel Lutheran Church.

attorneys.name: Shaniya Raheja
attorneys.practice_type: Audits Lawyers in Royal Oak, MI
attorneys.bio:
Shaniya Raheja is an associate attorney at Wachler & Associates, P.C. Shaniya represents healthcare providers and suppliers in a broad range of healthcare law, regulatory, and compliance matters, with a particular focus on Medicare audits and related appeals.

Shaniya graduated from the University of Notre Dame Law School, where she served as Vice President of the Real Estate Law Society and as a Lead Editor for the Notre Dame Journal of International and Comparative Law. She earned her B.A. from the University of California, San Diego, graduating in three years, summa cum laude with a concentration in Political Science and Public Law.

Prior to joining Wachler & Associates, P.C., Shaniya gained diverse legal experience across multiple sectors. Her background includes working in private equity at Foley & Lardner LLP, serving as in-house counsel at Summa Health and Cummins Inc., and completing internships at Clifford Chance and Reed Smith in Abu Dhabi. This broad exposure to corporate transactions, mergers and acquisitions, and international legal work informs her practical, business-focused approach to client matters.

With a foundation in M&A and private equity law, Shaniya brings a unique, business-oriented perspective to the complexities of healthcare law. Her understanding of how government agencies and private entities operate from an operational and transactional standpoint allows her to craft strategic, efficient solutions to sophisticated healthcare regulatory challenges.

Shaniya is admitted to the State Bar of Michigan.

Since joining our firm, Adam has gained experience in a variety of unique situations, including:

dividing condominium units and modifying condominium plans.

snowbird and off-site landlord issues.

sidewalk and driveway replacement.

working with wetlands preservation and green space restrictions.

drafting and granting permits.

drafting and reviewing deeds, leases and land contracts.

handling indemnification agreements.

litigating land contract forfeiture.

modifying insurance policies.

facilitating insurance repairs and reconstruction.

drafting, interpreting and administering shared maintenance agreements.

In his spare time, Adam enjoys building and modifying computers, and travelling with his wife Danielle.

attorneys.name: Michael A. Rataj
attorneys.practice_type: Federal Crimes Defense Lawyers in Detroit, MI
attorneys.bio:
My name is Michael A. Rataj, and I founded my Detroit law office in order to protect the futures of those charged with criminal offences in the Detroit metropolitan area, Wayne County and surrounding eastern Michigan. Because of my unique approach to criminal law, the residents of the Detroit area have turned to me for over 37 years as they face a range of criminal charges.

I began practicing law in 1989 after earning my law degree from what was then Detroit College of Law and my admission to the State Bar of Michigan. Since I began my legal career, I have earned a reputation for providing outstanding service to my clients. I was admitted in 2020 as a Fellow to the American Board of Criminal Lawyers. I have been voted by my peers as a Super Lawyer, and the National Association of Distinguished Counsel has designated me as a Top One Percent Lawyer. I have also been involved in numerous high-profile cases both in State and Federal Court. Having served in the United States Marine Corps, I bring a disciplined mindset, work ethic and attitude to the defense of those accused of crimes.

If you want an attorney who will treat you with respect and will provide aggressive representation, you can turn to the law firm of Michael A. Rataj, PC. I pride myself on treating all of my clients as if they were members of my family. This approach is unusual in criminal law, but it ensures that my clients receive the highest-quality representation that I can deliver. If you would like to learn more about the benefits of choosing my law firm, you can take advantage of my offer for a free initial consultation.
